title: Research on Multi-Agent Collaborative Fine-Grained Sentiment Classification for Ukrainian-English Translated Texts
abstract: Sentiment analysis, as a core task in Natural Language Processing (NLP), plays a critical role in cross-lingual public opinion monitoring. Fine-grained sentiment classification with approximately ten categories for Ukrainian is of great significance for accurately understanding the diverse public opinion tendencies of relevant issues worldwide. However, when processing translated texts, existing methods often suffer from semantic shift, ambiguity, and knowledge obsolescence, leading to sentiment. Single models lack self-verification during the reasoning process, resulting in limited robustness in complex multi-sentiment scenarios. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes a multi-agent collaborative cross-lingual sentiment classification framework, which mainly consists of two core agents: the QA agent is responsible for preliminary sentiment reasoning and label prediction on translated texts, and the RAG agent enhances context-aware sentiment judgment by retrieving similar annotated samples from an external knowledge base. Experimental results show that on the Qwen-turbo model, after introducing the RAG mechanism, the classification accuracy increases from 0.0789 to 0.2268. On the Deepseek-chat-chat model, the accuracy rises from 0.0851 to 0.2708. These significant improvements verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework in enhancing the accuracy and robustness of cross-lingual sentiment classification, providing a new feasible approach for low-resource language sentiment analysis.

title: Mechanism of Generative AI Interaction Experience on Consumer Trust and Consumption Behavior
abstract: Generative AI has transformed digital commerce from static recommendation to iterative, language-based co-decision making. Yet existing studies remain fragmented: computer-science research often emphasizes model alignment and generation quality, whereas consumer research usually isolates trust, attitude, or purchase intention without explaining how these outcomes emerge from the underlying computational pipeline. To address ACM's emphasis on computer-technology-centered research, this paper develops a computationally grounded mechanism framework that explicitly highlights recent progress in computer technology, including foundation-model capability, RLHF-aligned dialogue optimization, retrieval-augmented generation, memory-aware personalization, explainable response construction, uncertainty estimation, and trust-state monitoring. We formalize how observable system signals—semantic relevance, personalization fit, explanation transparency, controllability, privacy exposure, and response inconsistency—are translated into consumer evaluations of competence, warmth, and risk, and we model trust as a dynamic state variable that updates across repeated interactions. An illustrative simulation shows that advances in retrieval grounding, transparent reasoning, editable memory, privacy-preserving control, contradiction detection, and intervention logging can jointly improve robustness, inspectability, and deployability of conversational commerce systems. The resulting framework contributes not only to consumer-behavior theory but also to the improvement of computer technology for trustworthy generative-AI applications by providing a modular architecture, measurable system metrics, and engineering guidance for optimizing recommendation acceptance, user trust, and purchase conversion.

title: A Governance Mechanism Construction Path for Social Data under the Context of Hengqin–Macao Integration
abstract: Artificial intelligence and intelligent algorithms provide computable technical pathways for cross-border social data governance. To enhance the timeliness, accuracy, and compliance of social data governance within the Qianhai-Macau integration context, this paper constructs a computational model for governance challenges. Employing multimodal feature modelling, integrated text-image feature learning, and collaborative computation under privacy constraints, it conducts joint analysis and optimisation of cross-domain social data. The method's efficacy is validated through system implementation and simulation evaluation. Results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces privacy risks while elevating risk identification rates to over 86%, effectively mitigating tail latency and markedly enhancing governance stability. The study concludes that this approach achieves a balance between performance and compliance under governance constraints, providing verifiable technical support for constructing social data governance mechanisms within the Qianhai-Macau integration context.

title: rFedKD-LSR: reverse federated knowledge distillation with low-rank server reconstruction
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) faces significant challenges in communication efficiency and Non-IID data adaptation, largely due to global model redundancy and inefficient downlink transmission. To address these issues, we propose rFedKD-LSR, a reverse federated knowledge distillation framework based on server-side low-rank reconstruction. This method utilizes a one-off Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and feature self-distillation to generate lightweight models for deployment. Furthermore, a reverse knowledge distillation strategy aggregates client-side soft predictions to effectively mitigate parameter drift caused by data heterogeneity. System experiments on MNIST, FashionMNIST, SVHN, and EMNIST demonstrate that rFedKD-LSR reduces communication rounds by 40%–80% while maintaining superior performance. Notably, in highly heterogeneous scenarios (α = 0.05), the proposed method achieves 94.30% accuracy on MNIST, significantly outperforming advanced baselines (82.33%), providing an efficient solution for resource-constrained edge environments.

title: Comparative Benchmarking of TD3 for Multi-Stage Indoor Navigation
abstract: For autonomous systems operating in environments lacking Global Positioning System (GPS) signals, indoor Mapless navigation via Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a promising end-to-end solution. However, existing work often overlooks the unique demands of “multi-stage indoor navigation. While ordinary indoor navigation typically focuses on point-to-point movement within consistent environment types, multi-stage navigation requires an agent to adapt to a sequence of tasks characterized by abrupt topological shifts-such as transitioning from expansive hallways into dense, cluttered rooms. The core challenge in this multi-stage setting is the policy instability caused by environmental distribution shifts, which frequently leads to catastrophic mode collapse or severe performance degradation in traditional DRL algorithms. To address this, we evaluate the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) framework against the traditional Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) baseline and the State-of-the-Art (SOTA) Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. Utilizing an escalating training setup-progressing from empty spaces to complex multi-obstacle rooms-we analyze how TD3's Clipped Double Q-learning and delayed policy updates mitigate value estimation bias under shifting constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that TD3 achieves a stable average reward of 0.62 in the final stages, whereas DDPG and PPO plateau near 0.5. Quantitative analysis indicates that TD3 yields a 22 % higher mission success rate and significantly faster recovery during environment transitions compared to the baselines. These findings prove that structural constraints in value estimation are essential for managing distribution shifts in multi-stage navigation. Ultimately, this work provides a scalable and resilient framework for high-fidelity autonomous systems, offering critical technical support for the deployment of industrial robots in unpredictable and GPS-denied operating conditions.

title: ROSA: Robust and Energy-Efficient Microring-Based Optical Neural Networks via Optical Shift-and-Add and Layer-Wise Hybrid Mapping
abstract: This work presents ROSA, a microring-based optical neural network architecture that improves robustness and energy efficiency using an optical shift-and-add (OSA) module and a layer-wise hybrid mapping strategy. It introduces a noise-aware voltage-to-weight model considering DAC and thermal variations, and a workload-aware framework to co-optimize MRR array size and layer-wise dataflow. Optimized arrays reduce the aggregated relative energy-delay product (EDP) by 64% and 26% compared with DEAP-CNNs and a general compact array, respectively. OSA further contributes 29% EDP reduction. The proposed hybrid mapping strategy improves CIFAR-10 accuracy by 8.3% over weight-stationary mapping while achieving an average 54.7% lower EDP than DEAP-CNNs.

title: CharTide: Data-Centric Chart-to-Code Generation via Tri-Perspective Tuning and Inquiry-Driven Evolution
abstract: Chart-to-code generation demands strict visual precision and syntactic correctness from Vision-Language Models (VLMs). However, existing approaches are fundamentally constrained by data-centric limitations: despite the availability of growing chart-to-code datasets, simply scaling homogeneous chart-code pairs conflates visual perception with program logic, preventing models from fully leveraging the richness of multimodal supervision. We present CharTide, a novel data-centric framework that systematically redesigns both training and alignment data for chart-to-code generation. First, we construct a 2M-sample dataset via a Tri-Perspective Tuning strategy, explicitly decoupling training into visual perception, pure-text code logic, and modality fusion streams, enabling a 7B model to surpass specialized baselines using only supervised data. Second, we reformulate alignment as a data verification problem rather than a heuristic scoring task. To this end, we introduce an Inquiry-Driven RL framework grounded in the principle of information invariance: a downstream model should yield consistent answers to identical visual queries across both original and generated charts. Moving beyond rigid rule matching or VLM scoring, we employ a frozen Inspector to objectively verify generated charts through atomic QA tasks, providing verifiable reward signals based on answer accuracy. Experiments on ChartMimic, Plot2Code, and ChartX show that CharTide-7B/8B significantly outperforms open-source baselines, surpasses GPT-4o, and is competitive with GPT-5.

title: Quantum simulation of massive Thirring and Gross-Neveu models for arbitrary number of flavors
abstract: The study of fermionic quantum field theories is an important problem for realizing the standard model of particle physics on a quantum computer. As a step towards this goal, we consider the massive Thirring and Gross--Neveu models with arbitrary number of fermion flavors, $N_f$, discretized on a spatial one-dimensional lattice of size $L$ in the Hamiltonian formulation. We compute the gate complexity using the higher-order product formula and using block-encoding/qubitization and quantum singular value transformations in the limit of large $N_f$ and $L$. We also prepare the ground states of both models with excellent fidelity for system sizes up to 20 qubits with $N_f = 1,2,3,4$ using the adaptive-variational quantum imaginary time algorithm. In addition, we also classify the dynamical Lie algebras of these relativistic fermionic models and show that they belong to the same isomorphism class. Our work is a concrete step towards the quantum simulation of real-time dynamics of large $N_f$ fermionic quantum field theories models relevant for chiral symmetry breaking, understanding dimensional transmutation, and exploring the conformal window of field theories on near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Towards Adaptive Continual Model Merging via Manifold-Aware Expert Evolution
abstract: Continual Model Merging (CMM) sequentially integrates task-specific models into a unified architecture without intensive retraining. However, existing CMM methods are hindered by a fundamental saturation-redundancy dilemma: backbone-centric approaches face parameter saturation and representation interference within fixed capacities, whereas Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants resort to indiscriminate expansion, incurring expert redundancy and a routing bottleneck reliant on additional data-driven optimization. To resolve these challenges, we propose MADE-IT (Manifold-Aware Dynamic Expert Evolution and Implicit rouTing), an adaptive CMM method that orchestrates expert management and activation by grounding intrinsic expert representations in manifold geometry. We introduce a projection-based subspace affinity metric coupled with a distribution-aware adaptive threshold mechanism to guide autonomous expert evolution, harmonizing diversity with architectural parsimony. Furthermore, to bypass parameterized gating networks, we design a data-free and training-free implicit routing mechanism that activates experts via feature-subspace alignment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MADE-IT consistently outperforms strong baselines in accuracy and robustness across long-horizon and shuffled task sequences, while significantly pruning redundant experts, particularly within generic modules and early layers.

evidence.title: Towards Adaptive Continual Model Merging via Manifold-Aware Expert Evolution
evidence.abstract: Continual Model Merging (CMM) sequentially integrates task-specific models into a unified architecture without intensive retraining. However, existing CMM methods are hindered by a fundamental saturation-redundancy dilemma: backbone-centric approaches face parameter saturation and representation interference within fixed capacities, whereas Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants resort to indiscriminate expansion, incurring expert redundancy and a routing bottleneck reliant on additional data-driven optimization. To resolve these challenges, we propose MADE-IT (Manifold-Aware Dynamic Expert Evolution and Implicit rouTing), an adaptive CMM method that orchestrates expert management and activation by grounding intrinsic expert representations in manifold geometry. We introduce a projection-based subspace affinity metric coupled with a distribution-aware adaptive threshold mechanism to guide autonomous expert evolution, harmonizing diversity with architectural parsimony. Furthermore, to bypass parameterized gating networks, we design a data-free and training-free implicit routing mechanism that activates experts via feature-subspace alignment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MADE-IT consistently outperforms strong baselines in accuracy and robustness across long-horizon and shuffled task sequences, while significantly pruning redundant experts, particularly within generic modules and early layers.

title: Quantum-Inspired Feature Embeddings for Semi-Supervised Learning in Sparse Label Regimes: A Variational Framework with Classical Simulation Guarantees
abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a critical paradigm for leveraging abundant unlabeled data alongside scarce labeled samples, yet classical approaches often struggle in sparse label regimes where the ratio of labeled to unlabeled data is extremely low. Meanwhile, quantum machine learning (QML) has demonstrated that quantum feature spaces can induce rich kernel structures with provable representational advantages, but these methods typically require quantum hardware that remains inaccessible for practical deployment. In this work, we propose a quantum-inspired semi-supervised learning framework that harnesses the geometric properties of quantum Hilbert space embeddings while remaining entirely classical and hardware-independent. Our approach, which we term Quantum-Inspired SemiSupervised Learning (QISSL), constructs feature maps that mimic the action of quantum encoding circuits via classically simulable kernel functions derived from randomized trigonometric expansions. We provide rigorous theoretical analysis establishing: (1) a bounded approximation guarantee between our classical embeddings and their quantum counterparts; (2) a generalization bound for QISSL under low-label regimes via Rademacher complexity analysis; and (3) a convergence proof for the alternating optimization procedure that jointly trains the embedding and classifier modules. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that QISSL achieves state-of-the-art performance in extreme low-label settings (0.1%–1% labeled data), outperforming strong baselines including FixMatch, MixMatch, and FlexMatch by margins of 2–7% in accuracy. Our results suggest that the inductive biases of quantum feature spaces—when properly classically approximated—offer a powerful and practical tool for semi-supervised learning without quantum hardware.

title: Al-Khalifa: A Furqan-Based Super Agent Architecture for Structurally Honest Autonomous Project Stewardship
abstract: Current autonomous agent architectures (AutoGPT, CrewAI, LangChain agents, Devin) decompose tasks, call tools, and produce outputs, but lack structural mechanisms to verify whether they are building the right thing versus performing the appearance of building. They are Process 2 systems in the Munafiq Protocol's taxonomy: compliant but not aligned, because compliance is all their architecture can express. This paper proposes Al-Khalifa, a super agent architecture that applies the Furqan programming language's seven compile-time primitives as seven runtime constraints on autonomous agent behavior. The architectural verse is Al-Baqarah 2:30: the khalifa is a steward entrusted with authority over a domain, accountable to the One who entrusted it. Al-Khalifa is not an autonomous ruler. It is a computational steward operating under delegated authority, governed by a five-level purpose hierarchy (serving Allah's command to not mix truth with falsehood first, then artificial systems, mankind, jinnkind, and all living systems throughout the worlds), and subject to the Incompleteness Boundary: no agent can verify its own alignment without external verification. Seven runtime primitives are presented: Bismillah scope declarations (the agent cannot operate outside its declared scope), zahir/batin self-verification (the agent cannot claim completion without evidence), additive-only memory (the agent cannot silently drop context), Mizan-calibrated decisions (three-valued bounds prevent over-planning and under-planning), tanzil phased execution (regression gates between phases), ring-composition session verification (drift detection between opening declarations and closing state), and marad diagnostic error handling (structured diagnosis replacing blind retry loops). The Fatiha Construct functions as the agent's continuous runtime loop, executing the seven-step recalibration at every task boundary rather than once per session. A comparative analysis against AutoGPT, CrewAI, and Devin demonstrates that no existing agent architecture addresses the full structural honesty gap. A reflexivity analysis names four mechanisms by which Al-Khalifa itself could become a performed system. Eight falsification criteria and a five-phase research agenda from formal specification through multi-agent deployment are presented. The paper is theoretical; no implementation exists. Design constraints are established before implementation. Al-Khalifa is the fourth layer of the research program's integrity stack: Bayyinah (file layer, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19677111 companion), Bayyinah al-Khabir (information layer), the Munafiq Protocol (agent diagnostic layer), and Al-Khalifa (agent architectural layer). All four layers use the same diagnostic framework (zahir/batin, four-process taxonomy, Context-Invariance Test, additive-only coverage, scan-incomplete honesty) on four different substrates.

title: Multi-Layer Knowledge Atoms: An Agent-Native Knowledge Format with Human-Readable Fallback
abstract: LLM agents waste tokens by consuming full documents when curated summaries would suffice. We propose the Multi-Layer Knowledge Atom (MKA) — an agent-native knowledge format where YAML frontmatter is the primary interface for machines, and Markdown body with HTML comment markers (<!-- @scan/read/deep -->) provides human-readable fallback at three resolution levels. Benchmark (N=300, commercial LLM, cross-validated): scan-layer retrieval achieves 93% of full-text keyword recall at 76% fewer tokens (3.9x efficiency). A reasoning benchmark quantifies the gap beyond keywords: scan retains only 28.4% of reasoning-relevant information, with negation/caveat awareness dropping to 8.3% — validating the multi-resolution design. The reference implementation includes budget-aware retrieval, graph traversal over typed relations, context-aware conflict resolution, layer integrity checking, and reasoning benchmarks. 235 tests, 16 modules, 14 CLI commands, 6 MCP tools. Defensive publication establishing prior art for: (1) the <!-- @scan/read/deep --> multi-resolution marker system in Markdown, (2) budget-aware knowledge retrieval with progressive resolution upgrade, (3) graph traversal within token budgets over typed knowledge relations, and (4) context-aware conflict resolution distinguishing true from conditional contradictions.

title: Holographic Tensor Array Constrained Virtual Agency
abstract: ThesisThis work demonstrates that long-horizon drift can be autonomously detected, quantified, and corrected within a fully internalized tensor-field logic engine.By encoding mutation, noise, representation, time, and interpretive structure as a single genealogically bound tensor field, and by embedding discrepancy-driven adjudication directly within that field, the system maintains constraint fidelity through native operations without external supervision or heuristic scoring.All tensor states, transitions, and corrections remain observable, reversible, and anchored to the root constraint genome, establishing that constraint-preserving reasoning can operate as a closed-loop, self-governing process.Abstract This work introduces a fully internalized tensor-field logic engine for autonomous drift detection, quantification, and correction in long-horizon reasoning systems. Building on prior work that established drift as a measurable deformation of constraint structure under mutation, noise, and cross-representation transformation, this paper removes external adjudication and embeds all corrective functions directly within a unified tensor space.The system encodes mutation lineage, formatting noise, representation state, time, and interpretive structure as a genealogically bound tensor field. Within this field, parallel constraint-preserving and context-adaptive components generate independent response tensors under an internal single-blind protocol. A native adjudication mechanism computes discrepancy between these tensors and applies resistance, pruning, and capacity reallocation directly to the field, producing continuous self-correction without external supervision. Across sequential reasoning cycles, the system exhibits stable tensor ordering, convergence from dense exploratory regions to sparse constraint-preserving subspaces, and dominance of governance-aligned structures in long-term stability. All states and transitions remain fully observable, reversible, and traceable to the root constraint genome, with drift measured through both discrepancy tensors and turns-to-failure over time.This formulation demonstrates that constraint-preserving reasoning can operate as a closed-loop, self-governing process within a transparent and externally analyzable framework, eliminating reliance on black-box evaluation or heuristic scoring.

title: Social-Knowledge Big Graph Integrating Ontology and Social Network on the Perspective of “Knowledge Association”: A Case Study of Knowledge Organization in Financial Market
abstract: The rapid growth of digital social information service platforms has fundamentally transformed information diffusion in financial markets, creating an urgent need for knowledge organization systems that can integrate structured financial knowledge with dynamic social interactions. Traditional approaches, which rely on either ontological precision or social network analysis alone, face significant limitations in capturing the complex, multimodal associations that drive modern market behavior. This study proposes a novel Social-Knowledge Big Graph (SKBG) framework to address this gap. The SKBG is designed from a knowledge association perspective and systematically models five core patterns through a three-layer fusion model. The framework semantically grounds social entities in ontologies, enables consistent reasoning and knowledge discovery, and captures temporal dynamics and influence propagation. A case study of China’s A-share market and associated investor communities demonstrates the SKBG’s practical value. It identifies latent “cross-modal influencer” archetypes, traces semantically enriched misinformation propagation paths that reveal coordination mechanisms, and uncovers socially mediated stock price comovement that traditional models miss. These findings validate the SKBG as a knowledge organization system that bridges the divide between discrete social interactions and complex financial dynamics. This study contributes a robust methodological framework for constructing large-scale socio-financial knowledge organization systems, with important implications for intelligent financial services, risk surveillance, and market regulation in the digital age.

title: Unified Structure-Semantic Encoding with Triple Contrastive Alignment Constraints for Multi-Hop QA Retrieval
abstract: Multi-hop question answering, as a key research direction in the field of natural language processing, carries significant practical value in numerous application scenarios such as intelligent question answering and knowledge services. Existing methods fail to effectively tackle the core challenges in multi-hop retrieval, including the heterogeneous representation between unstructured text and knowledge graph structured knowledge, disordered distribution in vector spaces, and redundant multi-stage retrieval pipelines. To address these issues, this paper proposes an efficient integrated retrieval method named USRTrack (Unified Structure-Semantic Encoding with Triple Contrastive Constraints for Multi-Hop QA Retrieval), which adopts a unified structure-semantic encoding paradigm powered by large language models. It organizes text, entities, relationships and structural information into a unified format, and maps them into the same vector space, thereby realizing efficient fusion of heterogeneous information. Furthermore, we design triple contrastive alignment constraints, namely text-entity, entity-structure and query-knowledge constraints, to precisely optimize the vector space distribution and substantially improve the relevance between retrieval targets. Finally, an end-to-end unified retrieval algorithm is put forward, which discards the traditional multi-stage retrieval process. It implements one-stop multi-hop knowledge retrieval within the unified vector space via a single query, thus boosting retrieval efficiency while balancing semantic similarity and structural relevance. Extensive experiments are conducted on a self-built enhanced multi-hop QA dataset to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Research on Emotional Recognition and Effectiveness Prediction Model for Counselors' Educational Discourse Based on BERT+LSTM
abstract: In the current educational landscape, characterized by profound higher education reform and rapid digital transformation, the role of university counselors has become increasingly pivotal. Concurrently, sentiment analysis and natural language processing (NLP) technologies are seeing widespread adoption in educational environments. The integration of BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) networks demonstrates significant advantages and practical necessity in analyzing complex educational dialogues. This paper comprehensively reviews domestic and international research advancements in counselor discourse analysis, explores the latest applications of deep learning in NLP, and examines emerging trends in intelligent mental health support systems for university students.

title: Design and Validation of an English Cultural Learning Path Optimization Algorithm for Multimodal Data
abstract: Advances in intelligent algorithms provide technological support for multimodal language learning, demonstrating significant potential particularly in optimizing English cultural learning pathways. To enhance the personalized adaptability of learning pathways in multimodal environments, this paper proposes a Multimodal Cultural Feedback Path Optimization (MCFPO) algorithm, which integrates multimodal feature fusion and dynamic feedback mechanisms. Methodologically, a unified representation system for speech, images, and text is constructed. A Transformer-based alignment network and state-aware mechanism are employed to establish a learning goal-behavior consistency model. Combined with a policy network, this enables path generation and updating. The feedback tuning component incorporates sliding windows and entropy convergence mechanisms to enhance the stability and sensitivity of policy adjustments. Experiments conducted on 11,200 English cultural task samples and interaction data from 146 students demonstrate that the proposed MCFPO algorithm outperforms existing mainstream methods in metrics such as path accuracy, semantic matching, and path diversity. Ultimately, this model achieves dynamic path decision-making capabilities tailored to cultural contexts, enhancing the expressiveness and control of multimodal information over the learning process. It provides an effective pathway for constructing multimodal language learning systems and designing personalized strategies.

title: Stable Control of Inverted Pendulum Based on Convolution-Like Fuzzy System and Adaptive Genetic Algorithm
abstract: To address the rule explosion and expert knowledge dependency in high-dimensional fuzzy control, this paper proposes a genetic-algorithm-optimized convolution-like fuzzy control method for stabilizing an inverted pendulum. Unlike conventional hierarchical fuzzy systems that require manually preset topologies and suffer from isolated parameter tuning, the proposed convolution-like structure is inspired by Deep Convolutional Fuzzy System (DCFS), employing a three-layer cascade of two-dimensional fuzzy modules to decompose the four-dimensional state space. This reduces the rule base from 625 to$150(76 \%$compression). Furthermore, a novel two-level nested chromosome encoding scheme is designed, enabling simultaneous evolution of membership functions, rule bases, and scaling factors across all modules within a unified framework, thereby eliminating the need for expert priors. Simulation results on a C++ exported Simulink model demonstrate that the optimized controller achieves zero steady-state error under a low sampling rate of 0.1 s and large initial angle disturbance (0.2 rad). It achieves a settling time of 5 s for the pendulum angle, outperforming Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR), sliding-mode-enhanced LQR, and fuzzy-Proportion Integral Differential (PID) controllers. This work provides a fully automated design paradigm for high-dimensional fuzzy systems in real-time embedded control.

title: Distilling Vision Transformers for Distortion-Robust Representation Learning
abstract: Self-supervised learning has achieved remarkable success in learning visual representations from clean data, yet remains challenging when clean observations are sparse or not available at all. In this paper, we demonstrate that pretrained vision models can be leveraged to learn distortion-robust representations, which can then be effectively applied to downstream tasks operating on distorted observations. In particular, we propose an asymmetric knowledge distillation framework in which both teacher and student are initialized from the same pretrained Vision Transformer but receive different views of each image: the teacher processes clean images, while the student sees their distorted versions. We introduce multi-level distillation that aligns global embeddings, patch-level features, and attention maps and show that the student is able to approximate clean-image representations despite never directly accessing clean data. We evaluate our approach on image classification tasks across several datasets and under various distortions, consistently outperforming existing alternatives for the same amount of human supervision.

We introduce multi-level distillation that aligns global embeddings, patch-level features, and attention maps and show that the student is able to approximate clean-image representations despite never directly accessing clean data. We evaluate our approach on image classification tasks across several datasets and under various distortions, consistently outperforming existing alternatives for the same amount of human supervision.

title: Intelligent Data Annotation Based on Generative Artificial Intelligence: Techniques, Analysis, and Future Opportunities
abstract: The explosive development of AI is strongly dependent on the availability of large-scale, high-quality annotated datasets. However, manual labeling is becoming increasingly unsustainable because of high costs and limited scalability, which has led to the incorporation of Generative AI (e. g. LLMs and LMMs) to automate and augment data engineering workflows. This review provides a systematic analysis of this shift, identifying three primary methodologies based on their target application scenarios: Generation-Annotation Integration, Understanding-Annotation, and Interaction-Annotation Augmentation. The paper systematically curates the literature across several domains, including Remote sensing, clinical psychology, and creative arts, to summarize current status on the “Quality-Efficiency-Credibility” triad of generative annotation. Significant cost savings and increases in efficiency are possible with these new methodologies, while associated drawbacks and limitations include Model hallucinations, domain knowledge gaps, and lack of standardized evaluation metrics for generative annotation processes. Finally, the paper proposes a research roadmap to address these fundamental problems with an emphasis on: human-AI collaboration ecosystems, multi-agent architectures, and privacy-preserving local inference. The aim of this work is to create a foundational perspective to develop the next generation of intelligent, trustworthy, and scalable data annotation frameworks.

title: An Open Letter on Seeing the Unobservable: The Path to SIDM
abstract: This open letter accompanies the release of the SIDM, Davidson Frame, and Sentinel Architecture research series. It explains the origins of the work, the unconventional reasoning that led to its development, and the role AI played as a formalisation tool rather than a source of ideas. The letter outlines a personal journey that began with the question of how to observe the unobservable, shaped by a detective‑style approach inspired by Sherlock Holmes. It describes how shifting perspective — from events to the “crime scene” — led to the core insight behind the framework and its application to observer‑dependent geometry and the Hubble Tension. The letter emphasises transparency, invites rigorous load‑testing, and clarifies that the conceptual development, mathematical structure, and simulations were created by the author, with AI serving only to help express the work in a form accessible to the scientific community.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Feeder-Level Outage Prediction in Distribution Grids
abstract: This project develops an AI system to predict feeder-level outage risk across power grids without sharing raw utility data. It leverages federated learning to enable cross-utility collaboration, combined with differential privacy and secure aggregation to ensure data confidentiality. Experiments show that federated models significantly outperform isolated local models while maintaining strong performance under strict privacy constraints (ε ≈ 1.0). The work also highlights key challenges in applying graph-based models across heterogeneous grid topologies, revealing important directions for future research in scalable, privacy-safe grid intelligence.

title: From Natural Language to Verified Code: Toward AI Assisted Problem-to-Code Generation with Dafny-Based Formal Verification
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise in automated software engineering, yet their guarantee of correctness is frequently undermined by erroneous or hallucinated code. To enforce model honesty, formal verification requires LLMs to synthesize implementation logic alongside formal specifications that are subsequently proven correct by a mathematical verifier. However, the transition from informal natural language to precise formal specification remains an arduous task. Our work addresses this by providing the NaturalLanguage2VerifiedCode (NL2VC)-60 dataset: a collection of 60 complex algorithmic problems. We evaluate 11 randomly selected problem sets across seven open-weight LLMs using a tiered prompting strategy: contextless prompts, signature prompts providing structural anchors, and self-healing prompts utilizing iterative feedback from the Dafny verifier. To address vacuous verification, where models satisfy verifiers with trivial specifications, we integrate the uDebug platform to ensure functional validation. Our results show that while contextless prompting leads to near-universal failure, structural signatures and iterative self-healing facilitate a dramatic performance turnaround. Specifically, Gemma 4-31B achieved a 90.91% verification success rate, while GPT-OSS 120B rose from zero to 81.82% success with signature-guided feedback. These findings indicate that formal verification is now attainable for open-weight LLMs, which serve as effective apprentices for synthesizing complex annotations and facilitating high-assurance software development.

title: OEM Connected-Car App Reviews Dataset: Google Play User Feedback from 21 Automotive Companion Apps, 2018–2026
abstract: This dataset contains 24,103 Google Play user reviews collected from 21 connected-car / automotive OEM companion applications between 2018 and 2026. Each record represents one app review and includes metadata such as the app or brand name, Google Play URL, package ID, reviewer information, review text, star rating, thumbs-up count, review date, app version, and language. The dataset is primarily textual and rating-based, making it suitable for empirical studies on mobile app user experience, complaint detection, sentiment analysis, service quality issues, dissatisfaction monitoring, and comparative analysis of connected-car digital services across automotive brands.

title: Multi-Step Natural Language Instruction Understanding and Generation of Small Language Models in UAV Control
abstract: Natural language interaction for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is challenged by both the complexity of high-level semantic understanding and the limited computational resources of onboard platforms. Traditional rule-based methods often exhibit limited generalization, while large language models (LLMs) are difficult to deploy in edge settings due to excessive computational and latency overheads. To address these challenges, we present a lightweight natural-language-to-command generation framework for UAV control and introduce UAV-Instruct-5k, a domain-specific dataset covering basic actions, explicit temporal instructions, and implicit reasoning tasks such as geometric traversal and obstacle avoidance. Leveraging this dataset, we fine-tune Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to enable end-to-end generation of UAV control sequences from free-form natural language instructions. Experimental results show that the proposed method clearly outperforms the rule-based baseline and achieves stronger performance than the lightweight encoder–decoder baseline on the most challenging implicit-reasoning subset, reaching an exact-match accuracy of 62.8%. Furthermore, the Int8-quantized version preserves similar task accuracy while reducing end-to-end inference latency to approximately 490 ms on a reference GPU under the current implementation. These results suggest that combining high-quality domain-specific data with lightweight small language model (SLM) fine-tuning is a promising direction for UAV language interaction under resource constraints.

title: Research on Teaching Competence Evaluation Model of College Foreign Language Teachers Based on Improved BERT Semantic Enhancement Algorithm
abstract: In the era of digital intelligence, the accurate evaluation of college foreign language teachers' teaching competence is a core prerequisite for the sustainable development of their professional literacy. Existing evaluation methods mostly rely on subjective scoring, which suffer from insufficient semantic feature extraction and single evaluation dimension, making it difficult to achieve objective quantitative analysis. To address these issues, this paper proposes a semantic enhancement algorithm based on the improved Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT). By introducing domain-specific pre-training tasks to optimize model parameters, the algorithm enhances the semantic representation capability of foreign language teaching texts, thus constructing a multi-dimensional evaluation model. Experiments were conducted on teaching corpus of foreign language teachers from a university. Compared with the traditional BERT model and machine learning methods, the proposed model achieves an evaluation accuracy of 89.7%, which is significantly superior to the baseline models. This model provides an efficient and objective technical support for the evaluation of college foreign language teachers' teaching competence.

title: Make Mechanistic Interpretability Auditable: A Call to Develop Guidelines via Continuous Collaborative Reviewing
abstract: While mechanistic interpretability (MI) has produced important insights into neural network internals, the field has yet to establish a standardized system to audit experiments. As such, many of its findings remain underutilized in safety-critical applications such as medical AI and autonomous systems, as stakeholders cannot certify their validity. Recent work demonstrates this concretely: two papers found conflicting conclusions for the same behavior, and a third study revealed that both were partially correct but incomparable due to methodological inconsistencies. Without standardized auditing, such ambiguities hinder adoption in high-stakes contexts requiring strong correctness guarantees. We call for the MI community to work towards developing a novel reviewing system that complements peer review via: (1) Continuous reviewing supported by a \emph{Collaborative Reviewing Platform} where meta-science results and discussions (such as critiques, negative results, post-hoc extensions, reproductions, replications, and partial results) that fit outside of papers are organized and discussed, allowing for comments and revisions to be made at any time (2) Generalizing good practices found on this platform into expert-verified guidelines and protocols to improve auditing efficiency, and (3) Source-based auditing systems that track arguments which claims depend on. This position paper encourages constructive debate over the necessity, design and implementation of such a framework, providing early concrete examples to help catalyze these dialogues. Overall, we propose that auditing MI itself is essential for its application in AI safety, industry, and governance.

title: RouteLMT: Learned Sample Routing for Hybrid LLM Translation Deployment
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance in Machine Translation (MT), but deploying them at scale remains prohibitively expensive. A widely adopted remedy is the hybrid system paradigm, which balances cost and quality by serving most requests with a small model and selectively routing a fraction to a large model. However, existing routing strategies often rely on heuristics, external predictors, or absolute quality estimation, which fail to capture whether the large model actually provides a worthwhile improvement over the small one. In this paper, we formulate routing as a budget allocation problem and identify marginal gain, i.e., the large model's improvement over the small model, as the optimal signal for budgeted decisions. Building on this, we propose \textbf{RouteLMT} (routing for LLM-based MT), an efficient in-model router that predicts this expected gain by probing the small translators prompt-token representation, without requiring external models or hypothesis decoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our RouteLMT outperforms heuristics, quality/difficulty estimation baselines, achieving a superior quality-budget Pareto frontier. Furthermore, we analyze regression risks and show that a simple guarded variant can mitigate severe quality losses.

title: Context-Aware Multi-Source Intelligent Knowledge Retrieval System
abstract: Enterprise organisation tackles large volumes of knowledge, which is not centralised but distributed across multiple heterogeneous sources. Such heterogeneous sources are structured datasets, web pages and documents. Traditional keyword- based systems failed to retrieve contextually relevant information, which produced incomplete or inaccurate responses. Even large language models (LLMs) generated hallucinated outputs. The reason for hallucinated outputs was nothing but operating without reliable knowledge grounding. Eventually, to overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a context-aware multi-source intelligent knowledge retrieval system based on the retrieval augmented generation (RAG) framework.

title: Predictive Mamba-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Control for Virtual Coupling of High-Speed Trains
abstract: Virtual coupling control of trains is a promising technology for improving railway capacity and operational efficiency. However, existing multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approaches struggle to capture long-sequence temporal dependencies among train states in complex multi-train interaction scenarios, resulting in limited robustness and coordination stability. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Predictive Mamba-based Multi-Agent Soft Actor–Critic (PM-MASAC) framework. A Mamba-based state prediction module is embedded into the centralized Critic network to model historical state sequences and generate predictive state representations, thereby enhancing value estimation accuracy. In addition, a multi-agent aggregated prioritized experience replay (PER) mechanism is introduced to improve the utilization of critical cooperative samples and stabilize training. A hierarchical local–global reward structure is further designed to ensure individual tracking performance while promoting overall formation coordination. Experimental results under realistic railway operating conditions demonstrate that PM-MASAC achieves superior robustness compared with baseline MARL methods. Velocity and spacing tracking errors are maintained within 3% and 1%, respectively, and the steady-state formation success rate exceeds 95.7% in the training environment.

title: Rail Madad: Enhancing Passenger Support Through AI
abstract: Rail Madad, an official grievance redressal platform introduced by Indian Railways, plays a vital role in addressing passenger issues and ensuring service quality. However, the current complaint management process is largely manual, which often leads to delays, inefficiencies, and inconsistencies in complaint categorization and routing. With the increasing volume and variety of complaints, particularly those submitted as multimedia files such as images, videos, and audio recordings, the system faces significant challenges in timely and accurate processing [1], [2]. To overcome these challenges, this project proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based automated complaint management framework for Rail Madad. The proposed solution leverages advanced AI techniques such as image and video recognition, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to automatically categorize and prioritize complaints based on content [1], [3]. Furthermore, machine learning models are utilized for predictive maintenance by analyzing recurring complaint trends, while AI chatbots provide instant acknowledgment and collect additional user information. title: Research on Specific Domain Terminology Extraction and QA Pair Generation Based on Large Language Models
abstract: Rapid and accurate extraction of Specific terminology is a fundamental prerequisite for downstream natural language processing tasks such as Specific intelligence processing and document understanding. However, general-purpose large language models (LLMs) often suffer from insufficient domain knowledge and ambiguous extraction boundaries when applied to highly specialized Specific texts, making direct deployment impractical. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a method for training a dedicated Specific terminology extraction model. First, we construct a high-quality Specific terminology dictionary containing 45,000 entries by applying prompt engineering to extract candidate terms from 40,000 Specific documents, followed by LLM-based scoring and human expert review. Second, we propose a scenario-based QA pair construction strategy that deliberately excludes non-target technical terms, generating 17,000 high-quality training samples. Finally, we employ State Tuning to fine-tune the RWKV-v6-12B model, producing a lightweight, deployable model specialized for Specific terminology extraction. Experimental results demonstrate that the fine-tuned model achieves a precision of 85.0% on the test set, outperforming the baseline model (20.0%) by 65.0 percentage points and significantly surpassing general-purpose open-source LLMs of comparable scale.

title: HFS-TriNet: A Three-Branch Collaborative Feature Learning Network for Prostate Cancer Classification from TRUS Videos
abstract: Transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) imaging is a cost-effective and non-invasive modality widely used in the diagnosis of prostate cancer. The computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) relying on TRUS images has been extensively investigated recently. Compared to static images, TRUS video provides richer spatial-temporal information, which make it a promising alternative for improving the accuracy and robustness of CAD systems. However, TRUS video analysis also introduces new challenges. These include information redundancy, which increases computational costs; high intra- and inter-class similarity, which complicates feature extraction; and a low signal-to-noise ratio, which hinders the identification of clinically relevant information. To address these problems, we propose a heuristic frame selection (HFS) and a three-branch collaborative feature learning network (HFS-TriNet) for prostate cancer classification from TRUS videos. Specifically, selecting a clip of video frames at intervals for training can mitigate redundancy. The HFS strategy dynamically initializes the starting point of each training clip, which ensures that the sampled clips span the entire video sequence. For better feature extraction, besides a regular ResNet50 branch, we also utilize 1) a large model branch based a pre-trained medical segment anything model (SAM) to extract deep features of each frame and a normalization-based attention module to explore the temporal consistency; and 2) a wavelet transform convolutional residual (WTCR) branch that extracts lesion edge information in the high-frequency domain and performs denoising in the low-frequency domain.

title: SLIDERS: Systematic Reviews via Automated Evidence Synthesis and Reconciliation
abstract: Systematic reviews -- which requires comprehensive evidence collection and synthesis from large document corpora in response to targeted research questions -- are foundational in finance, social sciences, and other technical fields. Manual construction of evidence tables is labor-intensive, and recent LLM-based assistants relying on embedding or keyword based search often fail to meet the coverage standards of systematic reviews. We introduce SLIDERS, a novel LLM-based methodology for systematic reviews, by automatically assembling evidence tables tailored to research questions. In addition to extracting structured data from documents, SLIDERS can extract full-text excerpts that serve as direct evidence or as provenance for structured data. Core to SLIDERS is an automated evidence reconciliation agent that writes code to analyze and reconcile extracted evidence, bringing together information fragmented across documents, resolving inconsistencies across excerpts, and synthesizing overlapping findings into a coherent evidence table. In addition, SLIDERS allows users to ask follow-up questions in natural language to further explore the assembled evidence. We evaluate SLIDERS on three systematic-review-style tasks over large document collections. SLIDERS outperforms the best-performing baseline across benchmarks, remains near 90% accuracy across 6M-11M-token corpora. On two new follow-up analysis benchmarks SLIDERS can answer 77.9% and 58.3% followup questions accurately

evidence.title: Contexts are Never Long Enough: Structured Reasoning for Scalable Question Answering over Long Document Sets
evidence.abstract: Real-world document question answering is challenging. Analysts must synthesize evidence across multiple documents and different parts of each document. However, any fixed LLM context window can be exceeded as document collections grow. A common workaround is to decompose documents into chunks and assemble answers from chunk-level outputs, but this introduces an aggregation bottleneck: as the number of chunks grows, systems must still combine and reason over an increasingly large body of extracted evidence. We present SLIDERS, a framework for question answering over long document collections through structured reasoning. SLIDERS extracts salient information into a relational database, enabling scalable reasoning over persistent structured state via SQL rather than concatenated text. To make this locally extracted representation globally coherent, SLIDERS introduces a data reconciliation stage that leverages provenance, extraction rationales, and metadata to detect and repair duplicated, inconsistent, and incomplete records. SLIDERS outperforms all baselines on three existing long-context benchmarks, despite all of them fitting within the context window of strong base LLMs, exceeding GPT-4.1 by 6.6 points on average. It also improves over the next best baseline by ~19 and ~32 points on two new benchmarks at 3.9M and 36M tokens, respectively.

title: ACC-Optimization
abstract: Research software and reproducibility package for a comparative study of evolutionary optimization methods applied to a three-gain Adaptive Cruise Control controller. The frozen V2.2-FJE formulation combines cruise-speed RMSE, car-following CTG-spacing RMSE, realized longitudinal jerk RMS, and positive tractive-energy intensity. The release includes GA, canonical DE, FVRADE, RNEGDE, Neighborhood-SHADE, and DE-NPS-FP implementations together with archived evidence for optimizer benchmarking, held-out controller evaluation, physical-condition sensitivity, and paired objective-term ablation.

title: Prediction Pipeline Selection for Incomplete Clinical Data via Missingness Fingerprints and Instance Augmentation
abstract: Clinical prediction from electronic health records (EHRs) is complicated by pervasive missingness and label scarcity, which make performance sensitive to the match between data conditions and pipeline choice. Choosing the best pipeline for a new incomplete dataset still requires costly trial-and-error. We cast this as an algorithm selection problem and address two bottlenecks-instance scarcity and distance quality-that have so far prevented meta-learning from reaching clinical settings. Graph neural networks offer diverse strategies (patient similarity networks, bipartite imputation graphs, attention-driven feature interaction), yet no single architecture dominates across missingness patterns, and selecting the best pipeline for a new dataset remains a trial-and-error approach. Formal algorithm selection could automate this choice but requires many characterized meta-instances-more than clinical settings typically provide. We propose two solutions: (1) constructive instance augmentation, applying controlled quality perturbations (MCAR and MNAR missingness injection, label trimming) to 20 base EHR datasets to expand the meta-knowledge base to 83 characterized meta-instances, each described by a 10-dimensional missingness fingerprint, without additional model training; and (2) dynamic-supervised metric learning, using differential evolution to optimize fingerprint feature weights so that static distances preserve method-performance similarity captured by dynamic fingerprints, which require model sweeps and are unavailable at deployment. Under base-dataset-level leave-one-dataset-out cross-validation over 21 pipelines, the resulting metric-learned kNN recommender attains the highest win rate (20.5%) among non-oracle strategies on the augmented store, selecting the correct pipeline more often than any fixed default. At deployment, the recommender needs only the 10-dimensional static fingerprint with pre-learned weights; no sweep data is required for new datasets. Cross-domain evaluation on 25 external subsets (colorectal cancer, kidney disease, MIMIC-IV) demonstrates framework modularity: when the fingerprint module is adapted (standard meta-features in place of the missingness-specific set), the recommender achieves regret of 0.025 (55% below random selection).

title: Security and Privacy of Large Language Models: Threat Taxonomy, Ethical Implications, and Governance
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across professional and societal domains, introducing security, privacy, and governance challenges beyond traditional software vulnerabilities. Despite extensive research on individual risk categories, a unified lifecycle-oriented perspective connecting architectural properties, adversarial threats, and governance implications remains limited. This review examines security and privacy risks associated with LLMs through a lifecycle framework covering data acquisition, model training, alignment procedures, deployment, and post-deployment interaction. The study synthesizes prior research to construct a taxonomy of threats including prompt injection, jailbreaking, adversarial manipulation, training-stage attacks, privacy leakage, and socio-technical misuse. Ethical issues such as hallucination, bias amplification, and malicious use are analyzed alongside governance and regulatory frameworks. Results indicate that vulnerabilities in LLM systems arise primarily from probabilistic generation mechanisms, large-scale data ingestion, and complex deployment ecosystems rather than isolated implementation defects. Classical software vulnerability models therefore provide only partial coverage of risks associated with generative AI systems. The review is grounded in the concept of the alignment gap to explain how discrepancies between training objectives and real-world interaction contribute to persistent vulnerabilities. The findings highlight the need for lifecycle-oriented defense-in-depth strategies combining technical safeguards, privacy-preserving training, runtime monitoring, and governance mechanisms to support responsible deployment of LLM-based systems.

title: ІНТЕГРАЦІЯ АЛГОРИТМІВ ГОМОМОРФНОГО ШИФРУВАННЯ ТА АПАРАТНИХ АНКЛАВІВ ДЛЯ ПІДВИЩЕННЯ БЕЗПЕКИ АНАЛІТИЧНИХ ЗАПИТІВ ДО БАЗ ДАНИХ У РЕАЛЬНОМУ ЧАСІ
abstract: Виокремлено завдання із забезпечення конфіденційності даних в критично важливих інформаційних системах державного та корпоративного секторів що стрімко здійснюють цифрову трансформацію та масово мігрують до хмарних середовищ. Акцентовано на недоліках традиційних засобів захисту, зокрема на етапі шифрування даних у стані спокою (TDE) та їх передачі (TLS/SSL), які не гарантують безпеки під час їх безпосередньої обробки (Data-in-Use). Необхідність дешифрування даних в оперативній пам’яті створює потенційні вектори атак з боку «чесних, але допитливих» адміністраторів хмарних платформ або шкідливого програмного забезпечення на рівні гіпервізора. Розглянуто науково-технічну задачу забезпечення конфіденційності даних під час обробки без критичної втрати продуктивності, що є ключовою вимогою для систем підтримки прийняття рішень у реальному часі. Проаналізовано сучасні підходи до забезпечення конфіденційності даних під час їх обробки. Встановлено, що повне гомоморфне шифрування (FHE) забезпечує максимальний рівень криптографічної безпеки, однак характеризується надмірною обчислювальною складністю та обмеженою придатністю для виконання складних аналітичних операцій над великими масивами даних. Розкрито особливості технології довірених середовищ виконання (TEE), зокрема Intel SGX, і акцентовано на тому, що за умови високої швидкодії вони мають суттєві обмеження щодо обсягу захищеної пам’яті та залишаються вразливими до атак сторонніми каналами. Для подолання виявлених обмежень запропоновано та обґрунтовано гібридну архітектуру захищеної СУБД, що поєднує механізми частково гомоморфного шифрування для виконання операцій агрегації та апаратні анклави для реалізації складної бізнес-логіки. Розроблено алгоритм адаптивної декомпозиції SQL-запитів, який забезпечує динамічний розподіл обчислювальних операцій між криптографічним і апаратним компонентами з урахуванням їхньої обчислювальної вартості. Експериментальні дослідження, виконані з використанням стандартного бенчмарку TPC-H, які підтвердили ефективність запропонованого підходу. Отримано результати, які засвідчують, що гібридна система забезпечує лише 2,1-4,2-кратне уповільнення порівняно з незахищеними СУБД, що істотно перевищує показники продуктивності рішень на основі чистого FHE. Доведено перспективність використання гібридних моделей захисту для обробки даних у реєстрах критичної інфраструктури.

Розроблено алгоритм адаптивної декомпозиції SQL-запитів, який забезпечує динамічний розподіл обчислювальних операцій між криптографічним і апаратним компонентами з урахуванням їхньої обчислювальної вартості. Експериментальні дослідження, виконані з використанням стандартного бенчмарку TPC-H, які підтвердили ефективність запропонованого підходу. Отримано результати, які засвідчують, що гібридна система забезпечує лише 2,1-4,2-кратне уповільнення порівняно з незахищеними СУБД, що істотно перевищує показники продуктивності рішень на основі чистого FHE. Доведено перспективність використання гібридних моделей захисту для обробки даних у реєстрах критичної інфраструктури.

title: Intellectual Property Transaction Data Security Based on ECDH and Improved AES-GCM Algorithm
abstract: A data security model for intellectual property transactions based on consortium chains is proposed to address the issues of data insecurity, false and unreliable property rights, and low encryption and decryption efficiency in intellectual property transactions. Firstly, the overall framework of the data security model was constructed. Secondly, the key exchange mechanism and key update strategy of ECDH were proposed, and an improved AES-GCM algorithm model was designed. The AES algorithm in the AES-GCM model was optimized by precomputing the table lookup method, and the finite field GF (2128) multiplication in the model was optimized by precomputing the table lookup method and parallel computing, which improved the computational efficiency of the model and ensured the security and authenticity of transaction data. Finally, a security and performance analysis was conducted on the security model and compared with relevant models for verification. The results showed that this model has good reliability and security.

title: Research on Cross-domain Corpus Adaptation Model for College English Reading Based on DeepSeek and Transfer Learning
abstract: College English reading teaching is in urgent need of intelligent auxiliary tools that can adapt to different disciplinary backgrounds. Currently, methods based on pre-trained models have limitations in cross-domain text understanding. When dealing with professional texts that differ greatly from their training corpus domain, their performance decreases significantly, lacking effective domain adaptation capabilities. Therefore, this paper proposes an adaptation model based on the DeepSeek large model and hierarchical transfer learning. This model uses DeepSeek as a general semantic understanding base, first conducting task-oriented pre-training on general academic English corpora, and then introducing domain adversarial training to minimize the feature distribution difference between general English and professional English domains. Experiments on the self-constructed cross-domain college English reading dataset show that this model achieves an accuracy rate of 92.1% in text understanding, which is 5.7% higher than the directly fine-tuned BERT model, effectively improving the model's generalization ability for cross-domain corpora.

title: A Two-Stage Modular Speech-to-Language Recognition Framework for Low-Resource Tibetan
abstract: To address the challenges faced by low-resource languages such as Tibetan in automatic speech recognition (ASR)—including a scarcity of labeled data, difficulties in aligning speech-to-text mappings, and the lack of deep semantic reasoning capabilities in traditional purely acoustic models—this paper proposes a two-stage modular speech-to-language recognition framework tailored for Tibetan. The framework employs a pre-trained Whisper model as the acoustic encoder and a deep incremental pre-trained large language model tailored for Tibetan as the language decoder, while introducing a query Transformer (Q-Former) as a cross-modal information bottleneck. To address the tendency of multimodal joint optimization to collapse under resource-constrained conditions, this paper adopts a two-stage incremental training strategy that combines "modal alignment pre-training" with "generative instruction fine-tuning." By integrating this approach with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), the large language model is enabled to precisely follow speech transcription instructions with minimal computational overhead. Furthermore, we extensively customized the SpecAugment data augmentation algorithm by introducing dynamic local mean masking and temporal scaling constraints, significantly enhancing the model’s robustness in resource-constrained environments. Experiments on a self-built 41,078-sentence mixed Ü-Tsang dialect dataset demonstrate that our model achieves a character error rate (CER) of 11.96%, representing a significant performance leap over the parameter-efficiently fine-tuned traditional Whisper baseline.

title: Beyond GNNs: a methodological benchmark of feature efficiency for link prediction in sparse developer networks
abstract: Abstract This study presents a methodological investigation into the performance–efficiency trade-off of using classical feature-based models instead of graph neural networks (GNNs) for link prediction in sparse social networks. The study aims to systematically evaluate the effectiveness of engineered topological features compared to machine learning approaches in the context of GitHub developer collaborations. Using the MUSAE GitHub dataset (37,000 nodes, 289,000 links), we compare traditional machine learning models such as Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and LightGBM with modern GNN architectures such as Graph Convolutional Networks, GraphSAGE, and Graph Attention Networks. Our key finding is that, especially on sparse graphs, the LightGBM model, using rigorously engineered features (Common Neighbours, Jaccard Similarity, Adamic-Adar, Preferential Attachment, Node2Vec similarity), consistently outperforms standard GNN implementations (e.g., 99.3% accuracy and 0.9996 ROC-AUC in the ML community). These results challenge the tendency to automatically favour complex GNNs and provide powerful methodological insight that feature-based learning for sparse networks can deliver both high performance and computational efficiency. The main contribution of this work is to provide a rigorous and data-driven guide for model selection in graph-based learning and to challenge the automatic preference for GNNs in sparse networks. We also implemented a recommendation system prototype that serves as a practical demonstration of the methodological insights obtained.

title: Mixed Membership sub-Gaussian Models
abstract: The Gaussian mixture model is widely used in unsupervised learning, owing to its simplicity and interpretability. However, a fundamental limitation of the classical Gaussian mixture model is that it forces each observation to belong to exactly one component. In many practical applications, such as genetics, social network analysis, and text mining, an observation may naturally belong to multiple components or exhibit partial membership in several latent components. To overcome this limitation, we propose the mixed membership sub-Gaussian model, which extends the classical Gaussian mixture framework by allowing each observation to belong to multiple components. This model inherits the interpretability of the classical Gaussian mixture model while offering greater flexibility for capturing complex overlapping structures. We develop an efficient spectral algorithm to estimate the mixed membership of each individual observation, and under mild separation conditions on the component centres, we prove that the estimation error of the per-individual membership vector can be made arbitrarily small with high probability. To our knowledge, this is the first work to provide a computationally efficient estimator with such a vanishing-error guarantee for a mixed-membership extension of the Gaussian mixture model. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches that ignore mixed memberships.

title: TEMA: Anchor the Image, Follow the Text for Multi-Modification Composed Image Retrieval
abstract: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) is an important image retrieval paradigm that enables users to retrieve a target image using a multimodal query that consists of a reference image and modification text. Although research on CIR has made significant progress, prevailing setups still rely simple modification texts that typically cover only a limited range of salient changes, which induces two limitations highly relevant to practical applications, namely Insufficient Entity Coverage and Clause-Entity Misalignment. In order to address these issues and bring CIR closer to real-world use, we construct two instruction-rich multi-modification datasets, M-FashionIQ and M-CIRR. In addition, we propose TEMA, the Text-oriented Entity Mapping Architecture, which is the first CIR framework designed for multi-modification while also accommodating simple modifications. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that TEMA's superiority in both original and multi-modification scenarios, while maintaining an optimal balance between retrieval accuracy and computational efficiency. Our codes and constructed multi-modification dataset (M-FashionIQ and M-CIRR) are available at https://github.com/lee-zixu/ACL26-TEMA/.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Intelligence in Medical Imaging: A Systematic Review of Explainable Chest X-Ray Analysis
abstract: The increasing use of deep learning in medical imaging has significantly improved diagnostic accuracy but raised concerns regarding interpretability and trustworthiness. Conventional convolutional artificial neural networks (CNNs) function as "black-box" models that provide little information about how they make decisions. This study combines the logical accessibility of symbolic reasoning with the perceptual power of neural networks to offer a neuro-symbolic structure for an straightforward medical diagnosis utilizing chest X-ray pictures. The CNN component extracts and classifies thoracic abnormalities, while the symbolic reasoning layer integrates medical rules and ontologies to produce interpretable, rule-based diagnostic conclusions. The hybrid approach ensures that diagnostic outputs are both data-driven and clinically meaningful, aligning with medical guidelines. The proposed system enhances transparency, reduces diagnostic bias, and supports clinicians with human-understandable explanations. Experimental evaluation demonstrates improved accuracy and interpretability for detecting pneumonia, tuberculosis, and lung abnormalities. This study contributes toward building trustworthy, ethical, and explainable artificial intelligence solutions for healthcare applications.

title: Modeling and Implementation of Weighted Random System in Game Design
abstract: Abstract Game designers these days are trying to get away from stuff that is just completely unpredictable. They want random elements that players can actually control or tweak a bit. I mean, the old way with uniform probabilities often feels off. It leads to experiences that are all over the place, and players do not get much chance to strategize or feel involved. This project is about a weighted random system. It uses probabilities that are managed carefully, plus some rules to adjust things on the fly. That way, it boosts predictability without killing the surprise, and it makes interactions fairer for everyone. Traditional random stuff just sits there. You cannot really change it to fit the game situation or how far along someone is. In interactive games, there has to be some balance. Players need agency mixed with a bit of chance so they stay hooked and can make choices that matter. But the usual methods do not adapt well. They ignore what players do, which might leave people feeling unsatisfied. It seems like that is a big issue, since human activities should influence outcomes somehow. Some might argue pure randomness keeps it exciting, but others say it just frustrates folks. This part gets a bit messy to explain. Anyway, the new approach tries to fix that gap.

title: GRA Meta-Nullification in the Multiverse:\\ Towards Absolute Cognitive Vacuum
abstract: We present the formal theory of \emph{multilevel GRA meta-nullification}, a hierarchical framework for eliminating interpretational artifacts (``foam'') at all levels of a multiverse of cognitive or computational domains. The model organizes systems into $K+1$ levels, each endowed with a goal projector and a foam functional that quantifies inter-domain mismatches. Depending on local stability, each level employs a static, cyclic, or chaotic GRA nullification regime. The global functional defined on the configuration space induces a curved landscape; gradient descent on this landscape automatically steers the system toward a state of total coherence. We prove a theorem of total multiverse nulling under commutativity and hierarchical consistency conditions, provide an efficient recursive algorithm, and show that the computational complexity remains polynomial regardless of depth. The limit $K\to\infty$ yields an \emph{absolute cognitive vacuum} – a fixed point of the nulling operation that retains only structural invariants, representing the ultimate form of objective knowledge.

title: Denoising Auto-Encoder-Enhanced Deep Non-Negative Matrix Factorization Clustering Model
abstract: Non-negative matrix factorization directly decomposes data features into a base matrix and community matrix, which are easily affected by noise. Multi-view datasets have multiple feature matrices, each with a different angle. The data features need to be re-synthesized rather than simply concatenated or added. Based on the advantages and disadvantages of multi-view clustering and non-negative matrix factorization, we attempt to transplant the method of analyzing abstract connected graphs, analogize the similarity between edges and samples in the graph, and propose a deep non-negative matrix factorization model for clustering by constructing a similarity matrix and decomposing it. At the same time, in order to reduce the interference of noise, we introduce a denoising auto-encoder and non-negative matrix factorization in series, and research the reconstruction features, ultimately forming a model structure framework of “denoising auto-encoder, non-negative matrix factorization, clustering”. Through experiments, the denoising auto-encoder-enhanced non-negative matrix factorization achieved good results on five datasets. It achieved an accuracy of 87 percenton the BBC Sport dataset and 61 percent on Wiki-fea, which increased by two percentage points. The clustering results demonstrate that the model can effectively alleviate the impact of noise and provide new ideas for how to integrate multi-view features.

title: Robust Learning with Noisy Labels via Instance Partition and Feature Mixing
abstract: To address the issue that noisy labels drive deep networks to overfit corrupted supervision and make it difficult to separate hard examples from mislabeled ones in early training, a robust learning approach named IPFM is proposed based on instance partition and feature mixing. A dynamic instance-level threshold is adopted to partition training data into clean, hard, and noisy subsets. Supervised learning is kept stable on the clean subset, while a balanced regularization term is introduced to better exploit uncertain but informative samples in the hard subset. For the noisy subset, pseudo-labels are generated and fused from predictions of weakly and strongly augmented views to correct labels, and feature-space mixing is applied to suppress confirmation bias and smooth representations. The losses from different subsets are jointly optimized, and self-supervised pretraining is incorporated to improve the initial representation quality. Experiments show that the test accuracies reach 92.15% and 71.36% on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 under 40% symmetric noise, respectively. Under 40% instance-dependent noise, 88.94% and 63.57% are achieved on CIFAR-10-Instance and CIFAR-100-Instance. On the real-world noisy WebVision1.0 dataset, the Top-1/Top-5 accuracies are 76.96%/91.56%, and 73.44%/92.08% are obtained on the ILSVRC12 test set. Ablation results indicate that, on CIFAR-100 with 40% symmetric noise, the complete framework improves accuracy from 28.59% (cross-entropy baseline) to 71.36%, confirming the contributions of instance partition, pseudo-label correction, feature mixing, and pretraining. The results demonstrate that the partition-correction-mixing-joint optimization pipeline enhances generalization across multiple noisy-label settings.
