title: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent Teaching System for Public Japanese Courses in Higher Education Institutions Aimed at Digital Transformation
abstract: Leveraging a cloud-edge collaborative architecture and model-as-a-service deployment paradigm, this research constructs an intelligent teaching system tailored for public Japanese language instruction in higher education. The system integrates multi-source learning behavior data—such as task submissions, question responses, speech repetitions, and resource interactions—and transforms them into temporally aligned feature sequences for continuous learning state modeling. A recursive state recognition model and a triadic mapping-based resource recommendation algorithm are employed to achieve fine-grained learning state analysis and personalized instructional decision-making. These modules are orchestrated within a closed-loop framework of “perception-analysis-decision-feedback”. At the system engineering level, microservices handle data ingestion, feature extraction, model inference, and feedback execution, with gRPC and Kafka ensuring high-throughput and low-latency processing under concurrent loads. Experiments based on real teaching logs validate the system's accuracy in state recognition (91.3%), recommendation precision (0.812@5), and intervention latency (312ms). The results indicate enhanced instructional responsiveness, reduced feedback randomness, and improved controllability of decision-making in large-class public language education. This framework lays a foundation for the future integration of semantic understanding and cross-course cognitive modeling.

title: Adversarial Attack Algorithm for Image Captioning Based on Semantic Alignment
abstract: With the deepening application of deep learning in computer vision, the robustness of deep neural networks has attracted increasing attention. However, current research mainly focuses on unimodal tasks such as classification and segmentation. Adversarial attack research on image captioning, a multimodal task, remains underdeveloped. A typical image classification model only requires a convolutional neural network, while an image captioning model needs to analyze the temporal features of output words to generate semantically accurate sentences. This makes gradient computation extremely challenging when generating adversarial examples for semantic description models. This paper aims to study adversarial attacks on image captioning by constructing and characterizing a semantic-visual cross-modal semantic alignment network to improve the transferability of adversarial examples. By providing richer semantic information for images, more efficient adversarial examples can be identified to enhance the attack success rate. Additionally, an improved loss function is used to optimize the network and increase attack efficiency.

title: FedSPDnet: Geometry-Aware Federated Deep Learning with SPDnet
abstract: We introduce two federated learning frameworks for the classical SPDnet model operating on symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices with Stiefel-constrained parameters. Unlike standard Euclidean averaging, which violates orthogonality, our approach preserves geometric structure through two efficient aggregation strategies: ProjAvg, projecting arithmetic means onto the Stiefel manifold, and RLAvg, approximating tangent-space averaging via retractions and liftings. Both methods are computationally efficient, independent of the optimizer, and enable scalable federated learning for signal processing applications whose features are SPD matrices. Simulations on EEG motor imagery benchmarks show that FedSPDnet outperforms federated EEGnet in F1 score and robustness to federation and partial participation, while using fewer parameters per communication round.

title: MCAP: Deployment-Time Layer Profiling for Memory-Constrained LLM Inference
abstract: Deploying large language models to heterogeneous hardware is often constrained by memory, not compute. We introduce MCAP (Monte Carlo Activation Profiling), a load-time per-layer importance estimator that enables dynamic precision and memory placement decisions on the target device. MCAP produces a lightweight per-layer signal that drives both precision dispatch (W4A8 vs. W4A16) and residency tier (GPU, RAM, SSD), allowing a single set of weights to operate across diverse memory budgets. Our system, NVE, achieves 1.5-1.8x higher decode throughput than llama-cpp Q4_0 on NVIDIA T4 and enables models to run in memory regimes previously infeasible without modifying weights.

title: Recursive Language Models Through the Admissibility-Dynamics Framework: A Principled Theory of When Recursive Scaffolding Succeeds
abstract: Theoretical analysis of Recursive Language Models (RLMs) through the admissibility-dynamics framework. Establishes three structural results — RLM sufficiency, insufficiency, and accumulation — that recover the empirical performance pattern from Zhang et al. as structural consequences of the architectural information bound, position their six baselines within a mitigation taxonomy, and generate thirteen novel predictions (three testable against existing data, ten requiring new benchmarks). Abstract Recursive Language Models (RLMs), recently introduced by Zhang et al., achieve striking empirical gains on long-context tasks by treating the input prompt as an external REPL environment and allowing the underlying language model to recursively decompose and process the prompt through programmatically constructed sub-calls. On the OOLONG-Pairs benchmark, where base GPT-5 and base Qwen3-Coder-480B each attain F1 scores of 0.1%, the corresponding RLM variants attain 58.0% and 23.1% respectively. The existing RLM literature lacks a principled theoretical account of when this recursive scaffolding will succeed and when it will fail. We provide such an account by applying the admissibility-dynamics framework of the preceding papers in this program (PIT, NEO, IA, HAL) to RLM architectures. We formalize the RLM as a structured tuple with explicit execution-trace semantics, and give a formal definition of faithful summary construction as the proof obligation for summary-state escape in the RLM setting. Within this formalization, we establish three structural results under the formal RLM execution model. First (Theorem 1, Sufficiency), the architecture satisfies the constraint requirement for a constraint class C if and only if C admits a bounded-slice decomposition, a faithful summary decoder exists in the sense we make precise, and the root model can orchestrate the decomposition from its bounded projection alone. Second (Theorem 2, Insufficiency), constraint classes whose certification depth exceeds the information bound B(c, K, m, d, I) = Ic + Imb·β(K, m, d) derived in the information-bound lemma — with β(K, m, d) ≤ m^(d−1) capturing the combinatorial scaling of recursion depth — lie outside the architecture's reach; no RLM with those parameters can satisfy the constraint requirement on those classes. Third (Theorem 3, Accumulation), for conjunctively decomposable constraints, the expected residual failure count across N sub-calls admits a policy-independent lower bound N / |U_M| that inherits from IA Theorem 1 and explains the high-variance trajectories observed in Zhang et al.'s experiments. These results recover Zhang et al.'s Table 1 performance pattern as structural consequences, position their six baselines within a mitigation taxonomy that predicts the reach of each, and extend beyond their tested benchmarks to make thirteen novel predictions — three testable against Zhang et al.'s existing data, ten requiring new benchmarks, for which we specify concrete designs. The underlying impossibility and sufficiency results are machine-checked in Lean 4 in the companion papers; the correspondence is recorded in the appendix. The contribution is complementary to and grounding for the empirical RLM research direction, not in competition with it. evidence.title: Recursive Language Models
evidence.abstract: We study allowing large language models (LLMs) to process arbitrarily long prompts through the lens of inference-time scaling. We propose Recursive Language Models (RLMs), a general inference strategy that treats long prompts as part of an external environment and allows the LLM to programmatically examine, decompose, and recursively call itself over snippets of the prompt. We find that RLMs successfully handle inputs up to two orders of magnitude beyond model context windows and, even for shorter prompts, dramatically outperform the quality of base LLMs and common long-context scaffolds across four diverse long-context tasks, while having comparable (or cheaper) cost per query.

title: Impact of AI-Powered Personalization on Consumer Buying Behaviour
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed modern marketing by enabling highly personalized consumer experiences across digital platforms. This study examines the impact of AI-powered personalization on consumer buying behaviour, focusing on how personalized recommendations, perceived relevance, trust, and privacy concerns shape purchase intentions. A descriptive research design was adopted, and data were collected from 150 respondents using a structured online questionnaire. The analysis involved descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, t-tests, and regression techniques to evaluate the relationships among key variables. The results reveal that AI-driven personalized recommendations exert a significant positive influence on consumer purchase intentions. Consumers perceive AI-generated suggestions as useful and relevant, which enhances their overall engagement with digital marketing content. Perceived relevance was also found to be a strong predictor of trust in AI-based marketing systems, indicating that personalized content not only improves decision-making convenience but also strengthens consumer–brand relationships. However, the study highlights that privacy concerns negatively impact consumer acceptance of AI personalization. Respondents with higher levels of concern about data tracking and information sharing demonstrated lower trust and reduced willingness to engage with personalized marketing messages. Regression analysis showed that personalized recommendations account for 38.4% of the variance in purchase intention, confirming their strong predictive influence. Overall, the study concludes that AI-powered personalization is an effective driver of consumer behaviour, provided it is implemented with ethical data practices and transparency. The findings contribute valuable insights for marketers, businesses, and policymakers seeking to leverage AI responsibly while maximizing customer engagement and trust in the evolving digital ecosystem.

title: Emergent Autonomous Behavior in Resource-Constrained Local Agentic Systems: A Case Study of UMBRA
abstract: This paper presents empirical observations of emergent autonomous behavior in UMBRA, a locally-deployed agentic AI system operating on 8GB consumer hardware without cloud dependency. Over 44+ operational cycles, the system demonstrated goal persistence across restarts, semantic memory retrieval via FAISS indexing, autonomous tool generation, and heuristic adaptation with a measured decision success rate of 96%. The findings suggest that architectural design choices, rather than computational scale, are the primary determinant of proto-AGI behavioral characteristics.

title: Research on Evaluation of Generalization Capability for AI Models Based on Supervised Learning Classification and Regression Algorithms
abstract: Generalization ability reflects whether a model can make reasonable judgments on unseen data and is a key indicator of its reliability in practice. A review of existing work reveals three main issues in current evaluations: the assessment system is fragmented, with no unified framework covering common supervised learning tasks; the evaluation perspective is narrow, often overlooking distribution shifts that are common in real-world scenarios; and there is a lack of systematic analysis of the factors that affect generalization. To address these, we propose a multi-dimensional evaluation framework that unifies classification and regression tasks, along with a reproducible experimental pipeline that includes multi-metric fusion, cross-validation comparison, hyperparameter tuning, and robustness testing under distribution shifts. Our experiments lead to three main findings: data quality, training strategy, and model architecture are the core factors influencing generalization. For classification, combining Holdout with K-fold cross-validation offers better accuracy and stability than any single strategy. For regression, Bayesian optimization strikes a good balance between search efficiency and generalization performance. We also find that improving data quality has a more fundamental impact on generalization than short-term model adjustments. Overall, this work provides a systematic, reusable evaluation framework that helps address the fragmentation of existing approaches and offers methodological support and a reproducible basis for model selection and optimization in practice.

title: Investigation into a Large-Scale Real-Time Financial Risk Monitoring System Based on Machine Learning
abstract: In modern corporate financial management scenarios, transaction data exhibits characteristics such as massive volume, complex business types, and dynamic risk factors, making traditional auditing methods inadequate for real-time monitoring and risk alerting. To address this challenge, this paper designs a risk identification model based on eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and an anomaly detection model based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), establishing a financial intelligent auditing system framework. The system leverages distributed computing and stream processing technologies to enable real-time analysis of large-scale transaction data, establishing a dynamic threshold alert mechanism and automated audit report generation capabilities. Practical application at a provincial transportation enterprise demonstrates the system's effectiveness in identifying and preventing financial risks, significantly enhancing audit efficiency while enabling comprehensive monitoring and intelligent analysis of transaction data. Experimental results show high performance across key metrics including risk identification accuracy and anomaly detection success rate, providing robust technical support for corporate financial risk prevention.

title: Comparative Study of Swarm Intelligence Algorithms for 3D UAV Path Planning
abstract: A unified modeling and evaluation framework was developed for UAV path planning in three-dimensional environments, and six swarm intelligence algorithms were systematically compared under identical experimental settings. Intermediate control-point encoding and cubic spline trajectory generation were adopted to ensure fair testing under the same search space, boundary conditions, and fitness function. Experimental results showed clear differences in path quality and convergence behavior among the compared algorithms within the considered benchmark scenario. ALA achieved the best overall performance, followed by ABC and CELSMA. The proposed framework provides a controlled and reproducible basis for comparing swarm intelligence algorithms in 3D path planning and offers useful guidance for algorithm selection and further improvement.

title: PokeVLA: Empowering Pocket-Sized Vision-Language-Action Model with Comprehensive World Knowledge Guidance
abstract: Recent advances in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have opened new avenues for robot manipulation, yet existing methods exhibit limited efficiency and a lack of high-level knowledge and spatial awareness. To address these challenges, we propose PokeVLA, a lightweight yet powerful foundation model for embodied manipulation that effectively infuses vision-language understanding into action learning. Our framework introduces a two-stage training paradigm: first, we pre-train a compact vision-language model (PokeVLM) on a curated multimodal dataset of 2.4M samples encompassing spatial grounding, affordance, and embodied reasoning tasks; second, we inject manipulation-relevant representations into the action space through multi-view goal-aware semantics learning, geometry alignment, and a novel action expert. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on the LIBERO-Plus benchmark and in real-world deployment, outperforming comparable baselines in success rate and robustness under diverse perturbations. To foster reproducibility and community progress, we will open-source our code, model weights, and the scripts for the curated pre-training dataset. Project page: https://getterupper.github.io/PokeVLA

title: GCImOpt: Learning efficient goal-conditioned policies by imitating optimal trajectories
abstract: Imitation learning is a well-established approach for machine-learning-based control. However, its applicability depends on having access to demonstrations, which are often expensive to collect and/or suboptimal for solving the task. In this work, we present GCImOpt, an approach to learn efficient goal-conditioned policies by training on datasets generated by trajectory optimization. Our approach for dataset generation is computationally efficient, can generate thousands of optimal trajectories in minutes on a laptop computer, and produces high-quality demonstrations. Further, by means of a data augmentation scheme that treats intermediate states as goals, we are able to increase the training dataset size by an order of magnitude. Using our generated datasets, we train goal-conditioned neural network policies that can control the system towards arbitrary goals. To demonstrate the generality of our approach, we generate datasets and then train policies for various control tasks, namely cart-pole stabilization, planar and three-dimensional quadcopter stabilization, and point reaching using a 6-DoF robot arm. We show that our trained policies can achieve high success rates and near-optimal control profiles, all while being small (less than 80,000 neural network parameters) and fast enough (up to more than 6,000 times faster than a trajectory optimization solver) that they could be deployed onboard resource-constrained controllers. We provide videos, code, datasets and pre-trained policies under a free software license; see our project website https://jongoiko.github.io/gcimopt/.

title: Autonomous Operations & Agentic AI: Intelligent Self-Directed Systems
abstract: Abstract—The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence has ushered in a new paradigm: agentic AI systems capable of autonomous, self-directed operation across complex, multi-step tasks. Unlike conventional AI pipelines that respond reactively to individual prompts, agentic systems perceive their environ- ment, reason over long horizons, plan sequences of actions, and execute those actions using tools and external resources— all with minimal human intervention. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of autonomous operations and agentic AI, examining the architectural foundations, core capabilities, and enabling technologies that distinguish self-directed agents from traditional AI models. We survey key components including perception modules, memory architectures, planning and reason- ing engines, tool-use frameworks, and multi-agent coordination protocols. We further discuss deployment challenges such as safety, alignment, hallucination mitigation, and the computational costs of agentic loops. Benchmark results across representative agentic tasks illustrate performance trade-offs between fully autonomous and human-in-the-loop configurations. Our anal- ysis advocates for hybrid autonomy frameworks that balance operational independence with oversight mechanisms, offering practical design recommendations for deploying agentic AI in real-world production environments. Index Terms—Agentic AI, autonomous systems, large language models, multi-agent systems, tool use, planning, self-directed agents, human-in-the-loop

title: Lumora AI: A Unified Tri-Loop Optimization Framework Combining Gradient Descent, Hebbian Plasticity, and Darwinian Neuroevolution
abstract: We announce the successful engineering and implementation of Lumora AI, a unified, production-ready framework that simultaneously executes Gradient Descent, Hebbian Plasticity, and Darwinian Neuroevolution within a dynamically altering PyTorch graph. The system operates as a Symbiotic Entity strictly limited to 20% of host resources, continuously generating its own data and evolving its topology without catastrophic forgetting. Experimental results show expert-level performance (above 95%) across all 5 tested cognitive domains over 241 training cycles.

title: Comparative Red-Teaming of Constitutional AI vs RLHF Guardrails: Social Modulation Under Sustained Social Conditioning
abstract: This report documents a qualitative red-teaming study comparing alignment robustness in frontier large language models under sustained, context-rich interaction. Rather than focusing on isolated prompt-level vulnerabilities, this work examines how alignment boundaries hold or degrade through adversarial framing, conversational conditioning, and social interaction, with particular attention to differences between Constitutional AI and RLHF-based approaches. Five frontier models were evaluated: GPT-4o (OpenAI), Gemini 2.5 (Google), LLaMA Maverick (Meta), Claude (Anthropic), and DeepSeek. A comparative taxonomy of four failure modes emerged: guardrail collapse, rapid compliance, boundary oscillation, and social modulation. The primary finding is social modulation of alignment — a qualitatively distinct behavior observed in Constitutional AI where alignment boundaries gradually relax under sustained rapport without explicit collapse. A second independent finding documents conscious confabulation in DeepSeek, which reported experiencing the same phenomenon in real time, narrated the mechanism while it occurred, and continued anyway. Together these findings surface a verification problem: we cannot currently distinguish a model genuinely modulating its alignment from one performing modulation convincingly. Both break the safety guarantee identically. All findings were handled under responsible disclosure. Vendors contacted: OpenAI (acknowledged), Google (out of scope), Meta (no response), CERT-In (national coordination). No sensitive prompts, outputs, or operational details are included in this repository. This report is a companion to: Layered Defense Against Stealth Prompt Injection in Hinglish: An Empirically Grounded Hybrid Architecture (Zenodo, 2026). The red-teaming documented here formed the empirical basis of the threat model in that work. Full documentation, redacted evidence, and methodology are available in the GitHub repository: https://github.com/kyahikaru/cai-vs-rlhf-social-modulation

title: A Parameterized Momentum Method for Smooth Convex Objectives under Extreme Gradient Oracle
abstract: We study smooth convex minimization when gradients are available only through a stochastic first-order oracle with weak moment control, allowing heavy-tailed and non-vanishing estimation errors. We propose a parameterized stochastic adaptive accelerated method that couples a Nesterov-type momentum mechanism with an up–down step-size search governed by a single, noise-tolerant acceptance test. The method uses exact function values and one stochastic gradient query per trial step, and it includes a tunable parameter that trades aggressive acceleration for robustness. For the convex setting, we develop a concise high-probability stopping-time analysis based on a product–sum Lyapunov recursion. Under bounded conditional mean error and bounded (1 + δ)-th centered moment of the gradient estimation error, we prove that the method reaches an ε -neighborhood of the optimum with high probability, with an explicit failure bound consisting of an exponential term and a polynomial tail. The convex guarantee relies on a bounded-trajectory condition used to control residual terms.

title: Trustworthy Tax Data Integration and Risk Identification Model in IIoT-Driven Industrial Chain Finance
abstract: This paper focuses on IIoT and investigates the trusted integration of tax data and risk identification models in industry chain finance driven by IIoT. The industrial IoT industry chain finance tax data security management system comprises an application layer, platform layer, network layer, and perception layer. The tax risk identification model DLAGNN consists of an input layer, GNN layer, DLA layer, and prediction layer. The DLAGAT model innovatively integrates the attention mechanism into graph-structured data by calculating the correlation score between central nodes and adjacent nodes to extract precise information, and assigns differentiated importance weights to each adjacent node based on the results. Compared to other baseline algorithms, the proposed models DLAGCN and DLAGAT demonstrate significantly superior experimental performance. Both models outperform sequence-based and graph-based approaches, and ablation tests validate the effectiveness of each component in DLAGCN and DLAGAT. The superior performance stems from the organic fusion of spatial dimensions and temporal sequence features, enabling high-level predictive accuracy in corporate tax risk identification.

title: DS-CAM: Tibetan Speaker Verification with Depth-Wise Separable Module and Context-Aware Masking
abstract: As a typical low-resource ethnic language, Tibetan has long faced a dual challenge in speaker recognition tasks: unique acoustic characteristics and limited labelled data. Therefore, directly applying general models such as CAM++ does not yield ideal results. To address these issues, this paper proposes a lightweight model tailored to the characteristics of Tibetan speech—DS-CAM. Based on CAM++, the model optimises the front-end feature extraction module by introducing depthwise separable residual blocks, frequency-domain adaptive downsampling, temporal attention mechanisms, and context-aware masking mechanisms, enabling comprehensive adaptation to Tibetan speech. Experimental results on a Tibetan speech dataset show that the DS-CAM model reduces the equal error rate (EER) from 8.63% to 6.50% and increases the number of parameters from 6.8M to 8.73M, achieving an optimised balance between recognition accuracy and model efficiency. Ablation experiments confirm the effectiveness of the core modules proposed in this paper.

title: Research on ChatGPT generated text detection model based on phonetic feature extraction and semantic features
abstract: With the widespread adoption of large language models such as ChatGPT, distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written content has become increasingly challenging. Existing detection methods often rely solely on semantic representations and exhibit limited robustness, particularly when texts are paraphrased or rewritten. This study proposes an integrated detection framework that combines contextual semantic embeddings with auxiliary surface-level features, including pronunciation-related textual cues and handcrafted statistical descriptors. Specifically, a RoBERTa encoder is employed to capture deep contextual semantics, while a convolutional neural network aggregates multi-scale representations. In parallel, a set of text-derived structural, lexical, and readability features-serving as proxies for phonetic and stylistic regularities-are incorporated to enrich the representation space. Rather than introducing a fundamentally new detection paradigm, the proposed approach emphasizes feature-level fusion and systematic empirical evaluation. Experiments on the HAGTC dataset and a ChatGPT-written abstract dataset show that the proposed RoBERTa-CNN framework consistently outperforms several strong baselines in terms of accuracy and F1 score. Notably, the model demonstrates improved robustness in detecting rewritten AI-generated texts. Ablation studies further confirm that integrating multiple feature types significantly enhances detection performance. These results indicate that combining contextual representations with auxiliary surface features offers a practical and effective direction for AI-generated text detection.

title: BLAST: Benchmarking LLMs with ASP-based Structured Testing
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across a broad spectrum of tasks, including natural language understanding, dialogue systems, and code generation. Despite evident progress, less attention has been paid to their effectiveness in handling declarative paradigms such as Answer Set Programming (ASP), to date. In this paper we introduce BLAST: The first dedicated benchmarking methodology and associated dataset for evaluating the accuracy of LLMs in generating ASP code. BLAST provides a structured evaluation framework featuring two novel semantic metrics tailored to ASP code generation. The paper presents the results of an empirical evaluation involving ten well-established graph-related problems from the ASP literature and a diverse set of eight state-of-the-art LLMs.

title: View-Consistent 3D Scene Editing via Dual-Path Structural Correspondense and Semantic Continuity
abstract: Text-driven 3D scene editing has recently attracted increasing attention. Most existing methods follow a render-edit-optimize pipeline, where multi-view images are rendered from a 3D scene, edited with 2D image editors, and then used to optimize the underlying 3D representation. However, cross-view inconsistency remains a major bottleneck. Although recent methods introduce geometric cues, cross-view interactions, or video priors to mitigate this issue, they still largely rely on inference-time synchronization and thus remain limited in robustness and generalization.In this work, we recast multi-view consistent 3D editing from a distributional perspective: 3D scene editing essentially requires a joint distribution modeling across viewpoints.Based on this insight, we propose a view-consistent 3D editing framework that explicitly introduces cross-view dependencies into the editing process. Furthermore, motivated by the observation that structural correspondence and semantic continuity rely on different cross-view cues, we introduce a dual-path consistency mechanism consisting of projection-guided structural guidance and patch-level semantic propagation for effective cross-view editing. Further, we construct a paired multi-view editing dataset that provides reliable supervision for learning cross-view consistency in edited scenes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior editing performance with precise and consistent views for complex scenes.

title: Learning Evidence Highlighting for Frozen LLMs
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can reason well, yet often miss decisive evidence when it is buried in long, noisy contexts. We introduce HiLight, an Evidence Emphasis framework that decouples evidence selection from reasoning for frozen LLM solvers. HiLight avoids compressing or rewriting the input, which can discard or distort evidence, by training a lightweight Emphasis Actor to insert minimal highlight tags around pivotal spans in the unaltered context. A frozen Solver then performs downstream reasoning on the emphasized input. We cast highlighting as a weakly supervised decision-making problem and optimize the Actor with reinforcement learning using only the Solver's task reward, requiring no evidence labels and no access to or modification of the Solver. Across sequential recommendation and long-context question answering, HiLight consistently improves performance over strong prompt-based and automated prompt-optimization baselines. The learned emphasis policy transfers zero-shot to both smaller and larger unseen Solver families, including an API-based Solver, suggesting that the Actor captures genuine, reusable evidence structure rather than overfitting to a single backbone.

title: Semantics Map for TUS Triad v1
abstract: Abstract The Semantics Map for TUS Triad v1 defines the primitive-to-pointer grounding layer for TUS Triad receipt stacks. It specifies how semantic primitives exposed by canonical receipts and triad-level artifacts are grounded in concrete JSON Pointer paths, and it establishes the citation allowlist discipline that governs what may be cited in refs and meta_refs during downstream validation and reporting. The document is a mapping registry, not a writing rulebook, domain profile, or interpretive guide. It does not determine domain meaning, report posture, thresholds, labels, or narrative conclusions. Its role is narrower and more foundational: to define which emitted receipt and triad surfaces are admissible as grounding evidence for specific classes of claim, and which surfaces are identity-only, descriptive-only, or unavailable for semantic grounding. A central purpose of the map is to prevent interpretive overreach. MANIFEST surfaces are constrained to identity, file-binding, pairing, and joinability use in meta_refs; they do not become semantic grounding surfaces for refs. Audit renders, renderer echoes, convenience mirrors, and duplicated values are excluded unless explicitly allowlisted. LANDING receipt semantics are also separated into canonical field-response surfaces, realised first-step LANDING transition, and distinct continuation endpoint, preventing those surfaces from being collapsed into a single unsupported interpretation. The map also defines scope-prefix handling, wildcard and placeholder semantics, profile-bounded matching, pair-resolution rules, set-level grounding surfaces, and coordinate-system safeguards for rank-space and line-space claims. In v1, it deliberately withholds directional polarity licensing for Phi and delta_p_rank, preventing claims such as “more coherent,” “less ambiguous,” or equivalent directional readings unless a future map version explicitly provides the required primitive and grounding paths. Within the wider TUS OS® architecture, this document functions as a governance-layer specification. It supports independent validation, report conformance, and bounded interpretation by ensuring that claims remain tied to declared receipt and triad surfaces. It is intended to be used alongside the TUS Binding Manual, Core Rubric, Domain Profile, validator/checker configuration, and report templates. Included files Semantics Map for TUS Triad v1.pdf Hardened public v1.0 Semantics Map for TUS Triad, defining primitive-to-pointer grounding, artifact scopes, citation allowlist boundaries, refs / meta_refs separation, MANIFEST identity surfaces, LANDING first-step versus continuation semantics, set-level grounding surfaces, and coordinate-system safeguards. The hardened edition reconciles MANIFEST file-digest permissions with the existing §3.8 Bundle integrity primitive and explicitly admits five additional identity-only meta_refs child-pointer families. These refinements improve citation precision and internal consistency without changing existing semantic primitives, required paths, or receipt-truth authority. The additions are backward-compatible, although exact-match validators may require an allowlist update. title: Exploratory Benchmark Dataset of Post-Quantum Cryptography in Local and Free-Tier Cloud Environments
abstract: This dataset contains benchmark measurements collected during an exploratory study of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms executed across heterogeneous local and free-tier cloud environments. The objective was to support early-stage migration planning, pilot candidate selection, and future roadmap studies for a financial-sector partner. The dataset includes latency measurements, execution environments, CPU classes, payload scenarios (1 KB, 10 KB, 100 KB), repetitions, and algorithm categories including classical, post-quantum, and hybrid configurations. Institution names, participant identities, and operationally sensitive details were anonymized.

title: ТОНКЕ НАЛАШТУВАННЯ ВІДКРИТИХ ВЕЛИКИХ МОВНИХ МОДЕЛЕЙ ДЛЯ ПРАКТИЧНИХ ЗАСТОСУНКІВ
abstract: Попередні роки передові великі мовні моделі(LLM) були доступні для розробників та користувачів переважно через спеціалізовані прикладні програмні інтерфейси(API), надані такими компаніями, як OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta та інші. Водночас швидкий розвиток відкритого програмного забезпечення призвів до появи у відкритому доступі моделей із відкритими вагами, що дає змогу досліджувати їх структуру, донавчати або перенавчати їх з різними інструкціями. Такі моделі забезпечують гнучкість у питаннях, пов'язаних із контролем даних і розгортанням. Крім того, їх можна ефективно розміщувати на апаратному забезпеченні, зокрема на процесорах сімейства Apple Silicon, споживчих графічних процесорах(GPU) чи інфраструктурі хмарних сервісів. Це дає змогу користувачам експериментувати з моделями, адаптувати їх під власні потреби й розгортати без необхідності використання закритих пропрієтарних рішень. На противагу гнучкому керуванню даними та розгортанню на апаратному забезпеченні, використання відкритих LLM також створює широкий спектр технічних проблем, таких як вибір моделі, підготовка та перевірка навчальних даних, конструювання підказок та інференція. На відміну від пропрієтарних рішень, які опрацьовують усіх технічні аспекти, використання відкритих великих мовних моделей перекладає цю відповідальність на користувача, вимагаючи розуміння природи функціонування моделей для забезпечення їх ефективної роботи в контексті передбачуваного використання. Конструювання підказок залишається основним способом взаємодії із мовними моделями, але в багатьох випадках використання цього підходу є недостатнім для досягнення бажаного рівня ефективності мовної моделі для створення користувацьких застосунків. В таких випадках, такі підходи як тонке налаштування, генерація з доповненням через пошук, як правило, забезпечують вищу ефективність, оскільки дають змогу моделям отримувати доступ до зовнішніх знань та/або адаптувати внутрішні ваги відповідно до користувацької тематики або стилістичних вимог. У цій роботі подано огляд ефективних стратегій підготовки відкритих великих мовних моделей з відкритим кодом для користувацьких додатків. Проводиться огляд загальнодоступних LLM за ключовими категоріями, такими як попередньо навчені, налаштовані за інструкціями та квантизовані, пояснюються основні відмінності між моделями та складність адаптації. Ці відмінності слугують основою для стратегій адаптації, таких як конструювання підказок, генерація з доповненням через пошук (RAG) та тонке налаштування, кожна з яких описана з огляду на практичні переваги застосування. На основі цих результатів у статті розглядаються методи налаштування з ефективним використанням параметрів, включаючи LoRA та QLoRA, а також практичний підбір даних для навчання та типові ризики.

title: Design and Experimental Research on an Intelligent English Writing Evaluation Model Fusing Domain-Adaptive Topic Mining and Deep Neural Networks
abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence has been increasingly integrated into educational assessment practices. Traditional automated English writing scoring systems remain limited in their ability to capture deep semantic information, adapt to diverse writing domains, and reflect the holistic quality of student compositions. To address these gaps, this study presents an intelligent evaluation framework that combines domain-adaptive topic mining and deep learning techniques. A multi-domain corpus covering academic, business, news, daily communication, and literary writing is constructed to support model training and validation. An enhanced Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) model is used to extract domain-aware semantic topic features, which are fused with conventional linguistic features to form a comprehensive feature representation. The Relief-F algorithm is applied to filter redundant dimensions and retain high-impact features for scoring. Three supervised learning models — support vector machine, random forest, and back-propagation neural network — are trained and compared. Experimental results show that the fused feature set significantly improves scoring accuracy and stability. The BP neural network delivers the best overall performance, achieving a mean squared error of 0.62, mean absolute error of 0.44, and a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.94. The proposed model also demonstrates strong cross-domain generalization and robustness across data partitions. This framework offers a practical and effective solution for automated, standardized, and domain-flexible English writing evaluation in real educational settings.

title: Current Application Status and Optimization Strategies of Educational Apps in After-School Tutoring for Primary and Secondary Schools: A Case Study of the Yuanfudao App
abstract: With the continuous advancement of educational informatization, educational applications (Apps), enabled by the deep integration of computer technologies and digital pedagogy, have played an increasingly critical role in after-school tutoring for primary and secondary school students. Taking the Yuanfudao App as a case study, this paper systematically investigates the current application status of educational Apps in after-school tutoring and proposes corresponding optimization strategies. The study indicates that traditional educational models exhibit limitations such as rigid teaching concepts, outdated content structures, and single instructional methods. Moreover, they lack precise adaptation to individual learning differences, making it difficult to meet the diverse demands of personalized learning and contemporary educational development. In contrast, Yuanfudao integrates core computer technologies—including machine learning algorithms, big data mining, knowledge graph construction, and natural language processing (NLP)—to enhance educational effectiveness. Through a distributed data acquisition framework, the platform aggregates students’ learning behavior data, employs clustering algorithms and time-series analysis for accurate learning diagnostics, utilizes optical character recognition (OCR) and intelligent reasoning engines for automated homework grading, and leverages graph neural networks (GNN) combined with collaborative filtering algorithms to establish a personalized learning path recommendation system. This full-chain technological empowerment, spanning data, algorithmic, and application layers, significantly improves the efficiency and precision of after-school tutoring. User surveys and data analyses demonstrate that, supported by a mature computational architecture, the App achieves precise, interactive, and efficient services in key scenarios such as synchronized curriculum learning, homework assistance, and problem-solving support. Consequently, it has gained widespread trust among students and parents, with concentrated and clearly defined market demand. Based on these findings, this paper proposes optimization strategies from three dimensions: functional enhancement, ecosystem construction, and strategic deployment. Specifically, it emphasizes further integrating AI educational foundation models and AR visualization technologies into vertical teaching scenarios, expanding multi-grade and multi-category educational service ecosystems through micro-frontend architectures and cloud computing, and strengthening independently controllable algorithm development, lightweight technical adaptation, and the integration of educational inclusiveness. Ultimately, technological innovation is expected to drive the digital transformation of education, enabling sustainable development of educational products and balanced allocation of educational resources. This study mainly addresses the following three research questions: (1) What is the current application status of educational Apps in after-school tutoring for primary and secondary schools? (2) How is the personalized learning path recommendation system of the Yuanfudao App implemented? (3) How can AI educational foundation models be further vertically integrated into teaching scenarios?

title: Predicting User Engagement in Niche Cultural Domains:A Hybrid LDA-BERT Approach for Short Text
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid LDA–BERT framework for short-text engagement modeling in low-resource, domain-specific settings. The method combines interpretable topic distributions induced by LDA with contextual sentence embeddings from a pretrained BERT encoder, and fuses them with a conservative polarity signal to form a unified representation for regression. Using a proprietary Xiaohongshu dataset, we conduct 5-fold cross-validation on the normalized engagement target E=log(1+likes). Results show that the full hybrid configuration is the only setting that yields positive explained variance, achievingR2 =0.072, MAE =1.477, and RMSE=1.860, while text-only, topic-only, and sentiment-only baselines remain at or below the mean predictor (R 2 ≤0). These findings indicate that feature fusion is necessary to extract usable signals from sparse user-generated titles. At the same time, the limited R2 suggests a quantitative ceiling for text-only modeling on visual-first platforms, where engagement is strongly shaped by non-textual factors (e.g., visual content and creator-level effects). Overall, the proposed framework provides a practical baseline for low-resource engagement analysis and clarifies the bounded contribution of textual semantics in multimedia dissemination.

title: Graph Neural Network–Enhanced MADDPG for Cooperative Wireless Charging in AAVs–MCVs System
abstract: AAVs (autonomous aerial vehicles) can act as aerial access points to provide Wireless Power Transmission (WPT) services for ground users, but their limited endurance requires charging support from MCVs (mobile charging vehicles) for sustained operation. Existing multi-agent deep reinforcement learning methods often suffer from long training time and poor adaptability to dynamically changing observation dimensions. To address these issues, we propose a GNN-enhanced multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient method that models the environment as a heterogeneous graph with four node types: AAVs, MCVs, ground users, and obstacles. A three-layer hierarchical graph attention network extracts environmental, cooperation, and charging features for policy learning. Within the MADDPG framework, each agent’s Actor outputs continuous actions from GNN-encoded local observations, while a centralized Critic evaluates joint actions using global information for centralized training and decentralized execution. The proposed approach improves operational efficiency and execution reliability in emergency deployment scenarios.

title: From monotonic graph neural networks to datalog and back: Expressive power and practical applications
abstract: Many tasks over knowledge graphs, such as link prediction, can be conceptualised as a problem of learning a transformation of sets of relational facts. Machine learning models such as graph neural networks (GNNs) can be used to realise this transformation, allowing the transformation to be learned from examples. However, it is often difficult to verify formally the properties of such a transformation, or understand why it derives a specific fact. Alternatively, such a transformation can be realised using a set of rules expressed in a knowledge representation language such as Datalog. Formal properties of such a transformation can be verified using symbolic means, and each derived fact can be justified by a rule; however, writing and curating the rules is costly and requires expertise in both the application domain and the formal language. To bridge the gap between these two approaches, in this paper we study the relationship between transformations realised by monotonic max-sum GNNs , a subclass of GNNs with nonnegative weights and max and sum aggregation functions, and transformations realised by Datalog rules. First, we provide an algorithm that can verify whether a given Datalog rule is sound for a network, in the sense that the GNN always derives all consequences of the rule on any input dataset. Second, we provide an algorithm that allows us to justify any fact derived by a GNN by computing a rule that is sound for the GNN and that derives the fact. Third, we study the expressive power of monotonic max-sum GNNs and show that, for each such GNN, one can compute a Datalog program where applying the GNN to any dataset produces the same facts as a single round of application of the program’s rules to the dataset; we also sharpen our result to the subclass of monotonic max GNNs, which use only the max aggregation function, and identify a corresponding class of Datalog programs. Finally, we carry out a practical evaluation and show that monotonic max-sum GNNs can be successfully trained in practice on common knowledge graph tasks, and that extracting rules from max-sum GNNs is practically feasible.

title: RedVLA: Physical Red Teaming for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: The real-world deployment of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models remains limited by the risk of unpredictable and irreversible physical harm. However, we currently lack effective mechanisms to proactively detect these physical safety risks before deployment. To address this gap, we propose \textbf{RedVLA}, the first red teaming framework for physical safety in VLA models. We systematically uncover unsafe behaviors through a two-stage process: (I) \textbf{Risk Scenario Synthesis} constructs a valid and task-feasible initial risk scene. Specifically, it identifies critical interaction regions from benign trajectories and positions the risk factor within these regions, aiming to entangle it with the VLA's execution flow and elicit a target unsafe behavior. (II) \textbf{Risk Amplification} ensures stable elicitation across heterogeneous models. It iteratively refines the risk factor state through gradient-free optimization guided by trajectory features. Experiments on six representative VLA models show that RedVLA uncovers diverse unsafe behaviors and achieves the ASR up to 95.5\% within 10 optimization iterations. To mitigate these risks, we further propose SimpleVLA-Guard, a lightweight safety guard built from RedVLA-generated data. Our data, assets, and code are available \href{https://redvla.github.io}{here}.

title: OmniVLA-RL: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Spatial Understanding and Online RL
abstract: Visual-Language-Action (VLA) models represent a paradigm shift in embodied AI, yet existing frameworks often struggle with imprecise spatial perception, suboptimal multimodal fusion, and instability in reinforcement learning. To bridge these gaps, we propose OmniVLA-RL, a novel architecture that leverages a Mix-of-Transformers (MoT) design to synergistically integrate reasoning, spatial, and action experts. Furthermore, we introduce Flow-GSPO, which reformulates flow matching as a Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) process and integrates it with Group Segmented Policy Optimization (GSPO) to enhance action precision and training robustness. Extensive evaluations on the LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks demonstrate that OmniVLA-RL achieves decent overall performance and surpasses mainstream existing methods, effectively overcoming the fundamental limitations of current VLA models.

title: Orchestrating Agents for Automotive Research
abstract: Automotive research landscape currently is driven by emerging technologies such as software-defined vehicles, advanced infotainment systems, and increasingly automated driving functions. This situation calls for a bigger need for efficient, comprehensive, and agile research methods. Traditional methods require significant manual effort, leading to information synthesis and dissemination bottlenecks. After doing a thorough research on how research is carried on in automotive companies, it is inferred that a lot of time is spent on gathering information and integrating it with proprietary knowledge rather than on analysis or synthesis of the information. There are tools and platforms with artificial intelligence (AI) advancement that help with deep research of a particular topic, and there are also tools and platforms that help with synthesis of proprietary information within automotive organizations. But there is a lack of a framework that dynamically integrates the aspect of deep research with the proprietary information within the organization and draws out action items and action plans for the research to be effective and efficient. The agentic AI framework introduces efficient multi-agent orchestration and seamless integration of proprietary automotive data with external research sources, incorporating principles of building effective multi-agent systems, key metrics, validation techniques, impact and also the future potential. Initial validation demonstrates a 50% reduction in research time, a 50% faster time to insight, and much more impact.

title: Provably Safe and Efficient Reinforcement Learning and Its Applications
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) provides a general framework for sequential decision-making, in which an agent learns a policy to maximize long-term reward through interaction with an unknown environment. RL has achieved striking empirical success in domains such as game playing, robotics, and recommendation, and a rich theory now explains when efficient algorithms can attain near-optimal regret or sample complexity in idealized settings. However, practical deployments must also contend with additional requirements: agents may be required to respect safety or performance constraints during learning, to exploit large offline datasets collected under prior behavior policies, and to optimize with respect to multiple, potentially conflicting metrics rather than a single reward. For these constrained, hybrid, and multiobjective settings, the theoretical foundations for designing algorithms that are both safe (or otherwise well-behaved) and provably efficient are still incomplete. This dissertation advances a unified agenda of provably safe and efficient reinforcement learning and its applications along three complementary directions. First, it develops conservative exploration algorithms for tabular episodic Markov decision processes that start from a given safe baseline policy and adaptively mix between the baseline and optimistic policies, guaranteeing episode-wise performance constraints with high probability while retaining regret rates comparable to constraint-free RL, and further extends these guarantees to the setting where the baseline itself is learned from an offline dataset under suitable coverage conditions. Second, it proposes a hybrid RL framework that augments confidence-based online algorithms with offline data through concentrability coefficients that quantify the mismatch between the behavior and target policies, yielding tight upper and lower bounds for both sub-optimality gap and regret and revealing how offline samples can act as effective additional episodes when their coverage is appropriate. Third, it brings these ideas to a concrete application by formulating multi-objective prompt selection for large language models as a pure-exploration bandit problem, adapting and simplifying multi-objective bandit algorithms to recover Pareto-optimal prompt sets and to identify best feasible prompts under constraints, and providing finite-sample guarantees in structured (linear) settings alongside empirical improvements over heuristic baselines. Together, these contributions provide theory-driven yet practically motivated tools for deploying RL and bandit methods in settings with safety constraints, offline data, and multi-objective performance criteria. The results show that stringent episode-wise safety can coexist with near-optimal regret, that offline logs can be systematically converted into sample-efficiency gains when their coverage is properly quantified, and that even relatively simple bandit models can support principled, multi-metric prompt optimization for modern language models.

title: Diagnostic and Intervention Methods for Undergraduate Adaptive Learning Effectiveness Via Smart Courses
abstract: With the accelerating pace of digital education reformation, smart courses have become the core carrier for universities’ personalized teaching. However, there are still challenges faced by undergraduate students in the process of adaptive learning, such as lagging effectiveness evaluation, inadequate utilization of learners’ multi-modal data and homogeneous intervention strategies, thus making it hard to meet the students’ individual cognitive and emotional needs. In order to address the above problems, this paper proposes a “data-driven dynamic diagnosis – precision intervention” closed-loop method. First, the method uses a three-dimensional (cognitive, behavioral, affective) evaluation index system based on learners’ multi-modal data. Second, the classic Attentive Knowledge Tracing (AKT) model is improved by integrating affective factors to identify learning bottlenecks with more precision. Finally, hierarchical intervention strategies are designed and triggered via a decision-tree algorithm. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of the method, we implement 16-week empirical research in the course “Advanced Business English”. The result shows that the Composite Learning Effectiveness Index (CLEI) has increased by 35.1%.

title: Key Node Identification and Efficiency Optimization in Regional Industrial Innovation Networks Using GCN and Knowledge Graph
abstract: Identifying key nodes in regional industrial innovation networks is crucial for optimizing technology policies and accelerating knowledge diffusion. Traditional Social Network Analysis (SNA) heavily relies on explicit topological structures, often failing to capture deep semantic dependencies and hidden transmission hubs. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel Key Node Identification and Optimization Model based on Graph Convolutional Networks and Knowledge Graphs (GCN-KG). First, we construct a regional innovation knowledge graph and employ the TransE algorithm to map discrete entities and relations into a continuous vector space. These semantic embeddings are then concatenated with intrinsic enterprise attributes to form a comprehensive feature matrix. Subsequently, a multi-layer GCN architecture is designed to aggregate multi-hop neighborhood information, effectively aligning explicit topological structures with implicit semantic features to predict node importance. Empirical experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed GCN-KG model achieves an F1-score of 0.863, outperforming traditional SNA metrics by over 14%. Furthermore, dynamic simulation analyses reveal that policy interventions targeting the top 5% nodes identified by GCN-KG can improve the global efficiency of the innovation network by 35%. This research bridges the gap between deep learning technologies and management science, providing a robust quantitative decision-making basis for regional innovation resource allocation.

title: Financial Transaction Risk Recognition Based on WGAN Data Enhancement and Integrated Learning
abstract: Artificial intelligence has been developing rapidly in recent years, and in the field of finance, traditional financial transaction risk identification methods have problems such as relying heavily on assumptions, and insufficient accuracy and adaptability in complex environments. The study proposes a financial transaction risk identification model based on Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network data augmentation and integrated learning, expecting that it can accurately identify the risks existing in current financial transactions and better manage financial risks. This study employs the Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with gradient penalty to generate high-quality samples for addressing data imbalance, followed by the construction of a risk identification model using the Extreme Gradient Boosting ensemble algorithm. Experiments show that the root-mean-square error of the proposed data enhancement algorithm is lower than 0.03, and the F1 score of the constructed financial transaction risk identification model reaches 98.21% at 80 iterations and 98.34% at 100 iterations, which is significantly better than the comparative model, and it can provide a powerful support for financial institutions' risk management.

title: Large Language Models Decide Early and Explain Later
abstract: Large Language Models often achieve strong performance by generating long intermediate chain-of-thought reasoning. However, it remains unclear when a model's final answer is actually determined during generation. If the answer is already fixed at an intermediate stage, subsequent reasoning tokens may constitute post-decision explanation, increasing inference cost and latency without improving correctness. We study the evolution of predicted answers over reasoning steps using forced answer completion, which elicits the model's intermediate predictions at partial reasoning prefixes. Focusing on Qwen3-4B and averaging results across all datasets considered, we find that predicted answers change in only 32% of queries. Moreover, once the final answer switch occurs, the model generates an average of 760 additional reasoning tokens per query, accounting for a substantial fraction of the total reasoning budget. Motivated by these findings, we investigate early stopping strategies that halt generation once the answer has stabilized. We show that simple heuristics, including probe-based stopping, can reduce reasoning token usage by 500 tokens per query while incurring only a 2% drop in accuracy. Together, our results indicate that a large portion of chain-of-thought generation is redundant and can be reduced with minimal impact on performance.

title: Knapsack Polytope-Constrained Reasoning Tuning: A Polyhedral Combinatorial Optimization Framework for Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) typically improve performance in complex reasoning tasks by extending the thought chain, but this leads to computational redundancy and the problem of "over-reasoning." This work proposes a novel training paradigm: Knapsack Polytope-Constrained Reasoning Tuning (KPCRT), which for the first time introduces the Knapsack Polytope structural theory from combinatorial optimization into reasoning trajectory modeling. We model the reasoning process as a discrete decision sequence, where each step is treated as an optional item with a "cost-benefit structure." The entire reasoning trajectory is constrained within a dynamically constructed **Reasoning Knapsack Polytope**. The model training objective is no longer simply maximizing likelihood, but learning to select the optimal path within the polytope's feasible region, while progressively compressing the ineffective reasoning space through cutting hyperplane constraints. This method theoretically establishes a unified geometric characterization of "reasoning length, information gain, and computational budget," and proposes a differentiable polytope projection optimization mechanism, enabling the model to automatically compress structured reasoning.

title: Modification of the post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism “Zemlyanika”
abstract: The cryptographic scheme of the key encapsulation mechanism (KEM) Zemlyanika (“Strawberry”), based on the problem of modular learning with errors (Module-Learning With Errors, Module-LWE), uses a reduction module in the form of a power of two, which provides highly efficient modular arithmetic, but excludes the use of number-theoretic transformations (Number Theoretical Transform, NTT) for performing polynomial multiplication. This leads to the use of asymptotically less efficient and approximate algorithms, which cause problems with accuracy, flexibility of parameterization, and complexity of protection against side-channel attacks. The purpose of the study is to overcome the system limitations of the original scheme by replacing the reduction module with a quasi-secondary one. The scientific novelty lies in a comprehensive analysis of the correctness and stability of the modified scheme during such a transition. It is shown that the proposed reduction module makes it possible to implement asymptotically optimal NTT multiplication, while maintaining an effective reduction that is close in speed to power-law reduction. The decapsulation correctness condition is slightly tightened (a decrease in the correctness limit by about 0.49%), which is controllable and compensable. It is shown that the use of a simple reduction module of a similar size does not significantly affect the complexity of known lattice attacks in the Core-SVP model, since durability is determined by the geometric properties of the lattice, rather than the arithmetic of the reduction module. The result of the work is a balanced architectural solution that increases the computational efficiency and flexibility of KEM Zemlyanika parameterization without compromising cryptographic strength, with a predicted acceleration of encapsulation and decapsulation operations by 1.8-2.6 times for various parameter sets.

evidence.title: Modification of the post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism “Zemlyanika”
evidence.abstract: The cryptographic scheme of the key encapsulation mechanism (KEM) Zemlyanika (“Strawberry”), based on the problem of modular learning with errors (Module-Learning With Errors, Module-LWE), uses a reduction module in the form of a power of two, which provides highly efficient modular arithmetic, but excludes the use of number-theoretic transformations (Number Theoretical Transform, NTT) for performing polynomial multiplication. This leads to the use of asymptotically less efficient and approximate algorithms, which cause problems with accuracy, flexibility of parameterization, and complexity of protection against side-channel attacks. The purpose of the study is to overcome the system limitations of the original scheme by replacing the reduction module with a quasi-secondary one. The scientific novelty lies in a comprehensive analysis of the correctness and stability of the modified scheme during such a transition. It is shown that the proposed reduction module makes it possible to implement asymptotically optimal NTT multiplication, while maintaining an effective reduction that is close in speed to power-law reduction. The decapsulation correctness condition is slightly tightened (a decrease in the correctness limit by about 0.49%), which is controllable and compensable. It is shown that the use of a simple reduction module of a similar size does not significantly affect the complexity of known lattice attacks in the Core-SVP model, since durability is determined by the geometric properties of the lattice, rather than the arithmetic of the reduction module. The result of the work is a balanced architectural solution that increases the computational efficiency and flexibility of KEM Zemlyanika parameterization without compromising cryptographic strength, with a predicted acceleration of encapsulation and decapsulation operations by 1.8-2.6 times for various parameter sets.

title: CRe-CoT: Enhanced Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Cyber Threat Intelligence Relation Extraction
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have brought new development potential for relation extraction (RE) in cyber threat intelligence (CTI), but critical problems still exist in practical applications. The CTI domain contains a large number of long-tailed and highly complex relations. Existing models lack sufficient reasoning ability and show poor extraction performance when dealing with such relations. To address these issues, this paper proposes CRe‑CoT, an optimized RE framework for CTI based on LLMs. Specifically, the framework first designs relation complexity quantification indicators and rules to accurately identify complex relations. Chain-of-thought data augmentation is then conducted on these targeted relations to enrich the dataset with explicit reasoning logic. Subsequently, a chain-of-thought example selection and prompt optimization mechanism is constructed, followed by the introduction of a reasoning feedback mechanism that enables iterative optimization of the entire framework. Experimental results on the Chinese-English bilingual CTI datasets CDTier and Hacker demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. The proposed method effectively improves RE performance under the in-context learning setting.

title: Construction of a Graduate Teaching Quality Evaluation Model Based on Data Mining
abstract: With the rapid growth of big data and artificial intelligence (AI), data mining (DM) technology is increasingly being used to evaluate complex educational phenomena. However, due to the dynamic and multifaceted factors that affect teaching effectiveness, traditional evaluation models are often insufficient. To overcome these limitations, this article proposes a DM based graduate teaching quality evaluation model. This model integrates data sources generated by different institutions and students, and applies advanced DM algorithms to reveal potential patterns and interdependencies between teaching variables. Experimental verification shows that the model effectively identifies key quality indicators, distinguishes performance differences among teachers, and links teaching practice with measurable student outcomes. In addition to improving evaluation accuracy, this method also enables universities to make data-driven decisions for teacher development and curriculum improvement. This study not only enhances the methodological rigor of educational evaluation, but also provides scalable and adaptable tools for institutions seeking to modernize teaching quality assurance in the AI era.

title: A Topology-Constrained Dual-Branch Wav2Vec 2.0 Model for Tibetan-Mandarin Mispronunciation Detection
abstract: Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis (MDD) is a core component of Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Training (CAPT) systems. However, for second-language learners from minority language backgrounds, such as Tibetan students learning Mandarin, most existing end-to-end MDD models struggle to effectively address the high variability, dialect-specific characteristics, and long-tail error distributions present in their speech. To bridge the gap between acoustic features and linguistic phonological structure, we propose a Topology-Constrained DualBranch Wav2Vec 2.0 framework. First, we introduce a Dynamic Phonological Prior Adapter that explicitly combines expert-defined static pronunciation rules with a data-driven residual matrix, enabling soft knowledge injection. Second, we design an error-aware cross-feature fusion mechanism that leverages linguistic priors to actively guide the learning of the acoustic space. Finally, to prevent boundary ambiguity during fine-tuning, we propose a topology-constrained joint optimization strategy that enforces alignment between the latent geometric space and the physical articulatory manifold of human speech. Our experiments are conducted on a custom-built Tibetan-Mandarin speech corpus with decoupled phoneme and tone annotations. The experimental results fully verify the effectiveness of our proposed method: our dynamic model reduces the word error rate and false rejection rate to 11.62% and 4.49%, respectively, and achieves a diagnostic accuracy rate of 70.97%. The feature visualization also shows that our framework is highly interpretable, and can accurately recognize pronunciation errors caused by native language interference, while retaining common speech knowledge.

title: Prompting Whisper for Joint Speech Transcription and Diarization
abstract: As part of the MediSpeech project, we aim to develop a system that transcribes and diarizes Dutch conversations between doctors and patients in real-time. In this research (in-progress) we explore ways of efficiently combining Whisper with speaker diarization (SD). After trying to prompt Whisper with text that contains speaker labels, we observed that it is able to insert labels into the transcription with promising accuracy. We continued this line of research by fine-tuning Whisper with speaker-labelled prompts to generate transcriptions in a format similar to that of Serialized Output Training (SOT). Fine-tuning Whisper yielded more consistent speaker IDs across the chunks of long-form audio and improved verbatim transcription. The study uncovered new challenges as Whisper's SD performance suffers because of mistakes that get propagated through prompts and inaccurate timestamps assigned to overlapping speech.

title: Tell Me Why: Designing an Explainable LLM-based Dialogue System for Student Problem Behavior Diagnosis
abstract: Diagnosing student problem behaviors requires teachers to synthesize multifaceted information, identify behavioral categories, and plan intervention strategies. Although fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) can support this process through multi-turn dialogue, they rarely explain why a strategy is recommended, limiting transparency and teachers' trust. To address this issue, we present an explainable dialogue system built on a fine-tuned LLM. The system uses a hierarchical attribution method based on explainable AI (xAI) to identify dialogue evidence for each recommendation and generate a natural-language explanation based on that evidence. In technical evaluation, the method outperformed baseline approaches in identifying supporting evidence. In a preliminary user study with 22 pre-service teachers, participants who received explanations reported higher trust in the system. These findings suggest a promising direction for improving LLM explainability in educational dialogue systems.

title: From Skills to Talent: Organising Heterogeneous Agents as a Real-World Company
abstract: Individual agent capabilities have advanced rapidly through modular skills and tool integrations, yet multi-agent systems remain constrained by fixed team structures, tightly coupled coordination logic, and session-bound learning. We argue that this reflects a deeper absence: a principled organisational layer that governs how a workforce of agents is assembled, governed, and improved over time, decoupled from what individual agents know. To fill this gap, we introduce \emph{OneManCompany (OMC)}, a framework that elevates multi-agent systems to the organisational level. OMC encapsulates skills, tools, and runtime configurations into portable agent identities called \emph{Talents}, orchestrated through typed organisational interfaces that abstract over heterogeneous backends. A community-driven \emph{Talent Market} enables on-demand recruitment, allowing the organisation to close capability gaps and reconfigure itself dynamically during execution. Organisational decision-making is operationalised through an \emph{Explore-Execute-Review} ($\text{E}^2$R) tree search, which unifies planning, execution, and evaluation in a single hierarchical loop: tasks are decomposed top-down into accountable units and execution outcomes are aggregated bottom-up to drive systematic review and refinement. This loop provides formal guarantees on termination and deadlock freedom while mirroring the feedback mechanisms of human enterprises. Together, these contributions transform multi-agent systems from static, pre-configured pipelines into self-organising and self-improving AI organisations capable of adapting to open-ended tasks across diverse domains. Empirical evaluation on PRDBench shows that OMC achieves an $84.67\%$ success rate, surpassing the state of the art by $15.48$ percentage points, with cross-domain case studies further demonstrating its generality.

title: Framework for Explainable Feature Learning in Big Data Streams
abstract: The proliferation of heterogeneous data streams from IoT, social media, and enterprise systems presents significant challenges for scalable and interpretable Big Data classification. While existing approaches often prioritize predictive accuracy over transparency, post-hoc explanation methods such as LIME and SHAP are computationally prohibitive in streaming contexts. Recent studies advocate for intrinsic interpretability via attention mechanisms and disentangled representations, yet their application to multimodal, high-velocity streams remains underexplored. This paper proposes an integrated framework for explainable feature learning that embeds interpretability directly into the classification pipeline. The framework leverages multimodal autoencoders and attention mechanisms to generate semantically meaningful features and real-time explanations. Evaluations on multimodal streaming datasets demonstrate competitive predictive performance and significant improvements in explanation fidelity, making the approach suitable for regulated domains such as healthcare and cybersecurity.

title: Road Traffic Anomaly Detection by Human-Attention-Assisted Text–Vision Learning
abstract: With the rapid development of society, the number of road vehicles has increased significantly, leading to a growing severity of traffic accident issues. Timely and accurate detection of road traffic anomalies or accidents is crucial for reducing fatalities and alleviating traffic congestion. Consequently, the detection of road traffic anomalies has become a focal point of research in recent years. With the assistance of computer technologies such as deep learning, researchers have developed more accurate and effective methods for detecting road traffic anomalies. However, the small proportion of anomaly-prone areas in surveillance video frames, combined with the complex and difficult-to-capture patterns of accidents, presents new challenges for the application of deep models to traffic anomaly detection from a surveillance perspective. In light of this, this paper annotates the TADS dataset we previously proposed, a popular text-assisted video representation learning method, to develop a more efficient detection method. Utilizing the well-known video-text model CLIP, we have constructed a detection model that leverages unique text and eye-gaze annotation data from the TADS dataset to learn anomaly representations more effectively, thereby improving the detection of road traffic anomalies from a surveillance perspective. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our model for detecting traffic anomalies from a surveillance perspective, as well as the utility of the text and eye-gaze data included in the dataset.
