title: ЕФЕКТИВНІСТЬ МАЛИХ LLM У СИСТЕМАХ ПЕРИФЕРІЙНОГО ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ
abstract: Це дослідження вивчає доцільність донавчання (англ. Fine-tuning) малих мовних моделей (англ. Small language models, SLM) для генерації навчальних завдань на мобільних пристроях. Зокрема, було донавчено модель Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct виконувати роль репетитора з англійської граматики для україномовних користувачів, здатного генерувати структурований, готовий до використання JSON-код із поясненнями рідною мовою. Високоякісні навчальні дані були згенеровані за допомогою GPT-4o та ретельно відфільтровані за допомогою підходу «LLM-як-суддя» (GPT-5.1) на основі спеціальних метрик (граматична плинність, наявність відповіді, різноманітність, складність, релевантність). Модель донавчалася з використанням методу LoRA (англ. Low-Rank Adaptation) через фреймворк Unsloth для забезпечення ефективності. Донавчена модель продемонструвала стрибок продуктивності порівняно з базовою версією: вона успішно перейняла бажану поведінку, послідовно надаючи пояснення українською мовою (завдання, яке базова модель провалювала у ~98% випадків). Донавчена модель досягла показника успішності 54% на наборі даних для тестування, порівняно з 2% у базової моделі. Тестування донавченої моделі виявило чіткі когнітивні обмеження, властиві масштабу у 3 мільярди параметрів: модель має труднощі з абстрактним визначенням граматичних тем. У складних реченнях із конкуруючими граматичними конструкціями, увага моделі часто cхиляється до сильнішого токена, ігноруючи цільовий об'єкт. Зрештою, ці результати ставлять під сумнів твердження про те, що ефективне міркування вимагає величезного масштабу. Зрештою, дослідження підтверджує, що стратегія «Розумних даних» (англ. Smart Data) дозволяє ефективно відокремити продуктивність моделі від кількості параметрів. Втім, зважаючи на ризик правдоподібних логічних помилок, пропонується впровадження таких моделей у парадигмі «Human-in-the-loop», де ШІ виступає генератором чернеток для фінальної верифікації експертом.

Smart Data) дозволяє ефективно відокремити продуктивність моделі від кількості параметрів. Втім, зважаючи на ризик правдоподібних логічних помилок, пропонується впровадження таких моделей у парадигмі «Human-in-the-loop», де ШІ виступає генератором чернеток для фінальної верифікації експертом.

title: BT-Planner: A Hierarchical Task Planning Framework for Robot using Large Language Models and Behavior Trees
abstract: Formulating highly robust and interpretable action plans is essential for enabling robot to reliably execute long-horizon tasks in real-world physical environments. While end-to-end Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer generalization, they suffer from black-box decision-making and high data dependence. Conversely, traditional Behavior Tree (BT) approaches provide interpretability but lack dynamic adaptability and automated generation capabilities. This paper presents BT-Planner, a novel hierarchical framework that synergizes the high-level reasoning of Large Language Models (LLMs) with the structured execution control of BTs. BT-Planner decomposes complex natural language instructions into a sequence of sub-tasks via an LLM-planner, which are then mapped to a reusable robot skill library and automatically synthesized into an executable BT defined in a parameterized XML format. A dedicated BT parsing and execution engine translates the XML into a runtime instance, driving the robot to execute tasks. Our method enhances explainability, facilitates skill reuse, and reduces data dependency compared to end-to-end approaches, while adding autonomy and flexibility over static BT designs. Experimental results demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness in managing complex, sequential tasks in dynamic environments.

title: Research on Labor Education Teaching Evaluation Model Based on Improved Faster R-CNN Model
abstract: In the context of intelligent algorithm-driven educational transformation, labor education, as a key pathway for cultivating students' practical skills, has garnered significant attention regarding its teaching quality. However, traditional teaching evaluation faces challenges such as ambiguous standards and lack of objective data support. Therefore, to address this issue, this study employs artificial intelligence to enhance algorithms and establish a scientific teaching evaluation model, providing an objective and accurate assessment standard for improving the quality of labor education. By integrating the characteristics of labor education classrooms, we improved the Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R- CNN) with the K-means algorithm, proposing an enhanced teaching evaluation model. Experimental results show that the improved Faster R- CNN model achieved an 88.40% to 94.50% increase in detection accuracy across test datasets, with detection efficiency reaching 15.2 per second—a 20% improvement over the original model. These findings demonstrate that the proposed labor education evaluation model is effective in addressing traditional assessment challenges, offering a novel methodology for evaluating labor education instruction.

title: SAS: Sparse Attention Synthesizer for Efficient Language Model Inference
abstract: Modern large language models rely on attention mechanisms that attend to all tokens in a sequence, resulting in quadratic computational complexity that limits scalability. While sparse attention reduces compute and memory requirements by attending to only important tokens, implementing these techniques presents significant challenges due to the complexity of combining static and dynamic sparse patterns and optimizing key-value (KV) cache management.

title: Optimization of interactive aviation speech generation model based on reinforcement learning
abstract: Speech synthesis technology aims to convert text into understandable speech, and its applications in fields such as aviation communication are increasingly widespread. However, traditional end-to-end acoustic models treat the “text-to-speech” mapping as a black box, ignoring the hierarchical physiological mechanism of human speech production, “language planning → physiological regulation → acoustic output”, which leads to weak model interpretability and performance limitations in low-resource or complex pronunciation scenarios. Meanwhile, pronunciation features, as the key physiological representation connecting text and sound, have great potential to improve the naturalness and robustness of speech synthesis, but their acquisition relies on expensive equipment and is difficult to directly obtain. Therefore, how to construct a high-quality speech generation model that can utilize the prior knowledge of pronunciation mechanisms and learn only from readily available text and audio data has become a key challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes an innovative interactive aviation speech generation model called HIPO-AM. The core idea of this model is to simulate the hierarchical process of human speech generation, by explicitly modeling the “physiological regulation layer” to enhance the interpretability and performance of the model. The model is mainly divided into two stages: The first stage is “Hierarchical Acoustic Feature Generation”, where the input text is mapped to pronunciation features through a deep neural network, achieving an explicit transformation from text to physiological actions; the second stage is “Feature Prediction and Optimization Based on Multi-task Perceptual Loss”, where an acoustic feature predictor is constructed, whose task is to directly predict high-quality acoustic features from the pronunciation features generated in the first stage. The innovation of this model lies in innovatively using pre-trained multi-dimensional discriminators (amplitude, phase, waveform) as fixed “quality assessment experts”, by calculating their internal feature layers’ perceptual losses and combining them with the basic regression loss to jointly guide the training of the predictor. This non-adversarial perceptual optimization strategy retains the ability to fine-grainedly supervise the quality of speech perception while avoiding the complexity and instability of GAN training. To validate the model’s effectiveness, extensive experiments were conducted on ARCTIC English corpora and THCHS-30 Chinese corpora. The results show that compared with multiple baseline models, HIPO-AM is significantly superior in multiple indicators. The subjective average opinion score (MOS) evaluation indicates that the synthesized speech of HIPO-AM has the highest naturalness and intelligibility scores, proving the high perceptual quality of the generated speech. In summary, the HIPO-AM model proposed in this paper effectively improves the accuracy and naturalness of speech synthesis through hierarchical modeling and perceptual optimization, providing an effective technical path for mechanism-driven high-quality speech synthesis, and has broad application prospects in fields with extremely high requirements for reliability and clarity, such as aviation communication.

title: A Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network for Dual-Scenario Electromagnetic Signal Recognition
abstract: To address the issues of weak local discriminative features, difficulty in modeling long-range dependencies, and insufficient cross-scenario adaptability in specific emitter identification (SEI) tasks, this paper proposes a multi-scale feature fusion network for dual-scenario SEI. The proposed method takes dualchannel one-dimensional radio frequency (RF) signals as input and integrates multi-scale strip convolution, hierarchical feature enhancement, and a deep bidirectional temporal reorganization mechanism to jointly model local fine-grained features and global temporal dependencies. In the radar SEI scenario, a simulated dataset with seven classes is constructed, where the proposed method achieves an accuracy of $91.71 \%$ and a Macro-F1 score of $91.70 \%$. In the public ADS-B communication dataset, using dual-channel log-spectrum features in the frequency domain as input, the proposed method achieves an accuracy of $97.41 \%$ on a 10-class classification task. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits strong recognition performance and cross-scenario adaptability in different SEI scenarios.

title: From Monolithic to Compositional: A Compositional Operational Semantics for Crystality
abstract: Parallel execution has become a key approach to improving blockchain scalability, but the lack of formal semantics for smart contract languages in such settings makes rigorous reasoning difficult. Crystality is a smart contract language designed for parallel EVMs, supporting scoped state and asynchronous relay across execution engines. This paper introduces a compositional operational semantics for Crystality. Unlike the original monolithic semantics, the new semantics decomposes the system into engine components and a global component, making the structure of parallel execution explicit. The compositional formulation enables simple proofs of key structural properties, including locality, global isolation, and strong commutativity of independent local steps. Furthermore, we prove that the compositional semantics is semantically equivalent to the original one via a transaction-level bisimulation theorem based on encoding and decoding functions between configurations, and two code-level bisimulation theorems for local and global execution.

title: Training Dynamics and Induced Preconditioning of ReLU Policy Gradient for Scalar LQR
abstract: Policy gradient is not invariant to reparameterization; the training dynamics of the weights of a neural controller differ from those of the induced gains. We make that difference exact for deterministic scalar discounted linear-quadratic regulation with bias-free one-hidden-layer ReLU policies. We show that policy gradient on the weights induces preconditioning on the gains' dynamics, alongside an explicit quadratic finite-step correction and an activation-group error. Moreover, we identify explicit conditions on the step sizes and initialization parameters that guarantee that the sequence of generated controllers remains stabilizing throughout training and converges to the optimal gains with high probability. For a given system and cost parameters, the sufficient step-size conditions imply contraction bounds independent of the network width. Numerical analysis illustrates how the neural realization changes the induced gain dynamics while maintaining stability across training.

title: π_{0.7}: a Steerable Generalist Robotic Foundation Model with Emergent Capabilities
abstract: We present a new robotic foundation model, called π_{0.7}, that can enable strong out-of-the-box performance in a wide range of scenarios. π_{0.7} can follow diverse language instructions in unseen environments, including multi-stage tasks with various kitchen appliances, provide zero-shot cross-embodiment generalization, for example enabling a robot to fold laundry without seeing the task before, and perform challenging tasks such as operating an espresso machine out of the box at a level of performance that matches much more specialized RL-finetuned models. The main idea behind π_{0.7} is to use diverse context conditioning during training. This conditioning information, contained in the prompt, makes it possible to steer the model precisely to perform many tasks with different strategies. It is conditioned not just on a language command that describes what it should do, but on additional multimodal information that also describes the manner or strategy in which it should do it, including metadata about task performance and subgoal images. This enables π_{0.7} to use very diverse data, including demonstrations, potentially suboptimal (autonomous) data including failures, and data from non-robot sources. Our experiments evaluate π_{0.7} across numerous tasks with multiple robot platforms, on tasks that require speed and dexterity, language following, and compositional task generalization.

title: TTS-PRISM: A Perceptual Reasoning and Interpretable Speech Model for Fine-Grained Diagnosis
abstract: While generative text-to-speech (TTS) models approach human-level quality, monolithic metrics fail to diagnose fine-grained acoustic artifacts or explain perceptual collapse. To address this, we propose TTS-PRISM, a multi-dimensional diagnostic framework for Mandarin. First, we establish a 12-dimensional schema spanning stability to advanced expressiveness. Second, we design a targeted synthesis pipeline with adversarial perturbations and expert anchors to build a high-quality diagnostic dataset. Third, schema-driven instruction tuning embeds explicit scoring criteria and reasoning into an efficient end-to-end model. Experiments on a 1,600-sample Gold Test Set show TTS-PRISM outperforms generalist models in human alignment. Profiling six TTS paradigms establishes intuitive diagnostic flags that reveal fine-grained capability differences. TTS-PRISM is open-source, with code and checkpoints at https://github.com/xiaomi-research/tts-prism.

title: A Computational Assessment of Solar Energy Potential in the Vidarbha Region Using PVLIB: Analysis of Irradiance and Solar Position
abstract: The global transition to renewable energy is critical for achieving energy security and mitigating climate change. The Vidarbha region of Maharashtra, India, possesses significant potential for solar energy generation due to its high solar insolation. This study presents a quantitative assessment of this potential by analyzing solar irradiance components and solar position parameters for Nagpur, the region's primary city. The research utilizes the Python- based pvlib library to simulate a Typical Meteorological Year (TMY). Key parameters calculated include Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI), Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI), Diffuse Horizontal Irradiance (DHI), solar zenith, and azimuth angles. Results indicate an exceptionally high annual average GHI of approximately 5.35 kWh/m²/day, with peak insolation during the pre-monsoon months. The analysis of the sun path confirms the necessity of optimizing tilt angles around 21° for fixed-axis systems. This study concludes that Vidarbha is a highly viable location for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) and concentrating solar power (CSP) projects. The pvlib framework proved effective for precise, location-specific resource assessment, providing critical data for engineers and policymakers to optimize solar energy deployment in the region.

title: A Working Language-Math Framework for Detecting Drift and Vacuum in AI-Affected Definitions
abstract: Langualgebra is a runnable language-math framework that replaces letter-based variables with number-based variables for conceptual analysis. In numerical algebra, letters can operate as variables because they are distinct from the numbers being manipulated. In Langualgebra, the inversion is intentional: language is already made of letters, so numbers are used as variables to reduce ambiguity when a language model is asked to reason over concepts, instances, suffixes, and transformed classes. Formula 001 is the first executable form of Langualgebra. It defines 01 as a reifiable concept, class, process, act, or artifact-category; 02 as a specific instance or manifestation of 01; a suffix as the affecting condition applied to the concept; 01 plus suffix as the affected class; and 02 plus suffix as a specific instance of that affected class. The suffix is not decorative. It is the operative transformation. The formula uses the suffix to unearth what 01 becomes when viewed relative to that suffix. In this version, the suffix is AI. Applying the formula to 01 = Technology produces 01AI = TechnologyAI: technology involved with or affected by artificial intelligence. This release includes TechnologyAI as the first complete execution of Formula 001. The report moves from the runnable formula, to specific AI-affected technology instances, to a class-level characterization of TechnologyAI. It identifies defining properties, structural changes, boundary conditions, internal tensions, and world-level implications of technology under AI involvement. TechnologyAI summary: This execution asks what happens to “Technology” when AI becomes the suffix acting on it. The result is that AI-involved technology is not merely ordinary technology with a new feature added. It becomes a different class condition: technology that can reason, generate, adapt, act, monitor, and sometimes improve or reconfigure itself. Traditional technology was mostly tool-like. A hammer, spreadsheet, database, or machine waited for human direction. AI-involved technology does not always wait. It can interpret intent, work across text, code, image, audio, video, data, and physical systems, continue tasks over time, and participate in decisions or actions that once required direct human operation. The report characterizes TechnologyAI through three main shifts: from feature to substrate, from deterministic operation to probabilistic behavior, and from operated tool to agentive system. These shifts create new pressures across software, hardware, energy, medicine, factories, science, security, labor, governance, and infrastructure. The central tension is that AI-involved technology moves faster than the human systems built to evaluate and govern it. Technical capability, deployment speed, and automation are accelerating, while law, ethics, oversight, institutional trust, and public understanding move more slowly. The result is not simply an upgrade to technology. It is a category shift in what technology is, how it behaves, and what must be named, evaluated, and governed. This version should be read as a conceptual working-paper upgrade and framework application. It does not claim final empirical exhaustion, legal classification, patent status, or absolute priority over all adjacent work. Its purpose is to establish a dated, citable formulation of Formula 001, Langualgebra, and the first complete suffix-affected execution for critique, comparison, refinement, and future validation.

It defines 01 as a reifiable concept, class, process, act, or artifact-category; 02 as a specific instance or manifestation of 01; a suffix as the affecting condition applied to the concept; 01 plus suffix as the affected class; and 02 plus suffix as a specific instance of that affected class. The suffix is not decorative. It is the operative transformation. The formula uses the suffix to unearth what 01 becomes when viewed relative to that suffix. In this version, the suffix is AI. Applying the formula to 01 = Technology produces 01AI = TechnologyAI: technology involved with or affected by artificial intelligence. This release includes TechnologyAI as the first complete execution of Formula 001. The report moves from the runnable formula, to specific AI-affected technology instances, to a class-level characterization of TechnologyAI. It identifies defining properties, structural changes, boundary conditions, internal tensions, and world-level implications of technology under AI involvement. TechnologyAI summary: This execution asks what happens to “Technology” when AI becomes the suffix acting on it. The result is that AI-involved technology is not merely ordinary technology with a new feature added. It becomes a different class condition: technology that can reason, generate, adapt, act, monitor, and sometimes improve or reconfigure itself. Traditional technology was mostly tool-like. A hammer, spreadsheet, database, or machine waited for human direction. AI-involved technology does not always wait. It can interpret intent, work across text, code, image, audio, video, data, and physical systems, continue tasks over time, and participate in decisions or actions that once required direct human operation. The report characterizes TechnologyAI through three main shifts: from feature to substrate, from deterministic operation to probabilistic behavior, and from operated tool to agentive system. These shifts create new pressures across software, hardware, energy, medicine, factories, science, security, labor, governance, and infrastructure. The central tension is that AI-involved technology moves faster than the human systems built to evaluate and govern it. Technical capability, deployment speed, and automation are accelerating, while law, ethics, oversight, institutional trust, and public understanding move more slowly. The result is not simply an upgrade to technology. It is a category shift in what technology is, how it behaves, and what must be named, evaluated, and governed. This version should be read as a conceptual working-paper upgrade and framework application. It does not claim final empirical exhaustion, legal classification, patent status, or absolute priority over all adjacent work. Its purpose is to establish a dated, citable formulation of Formula 001, Langualgebra, and the first complete suffix-affected execution for critique, comparison, refinement, and future validation.

title: Research on UAV Path Planning Based on Enhanced Artificial Lemming Algorithm
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle path planning faces multiple challenges in terms of effectiveness and safety. Traditional optimization methods are difficult to use to effectively find the best route. An enhanced artificial lemming optimization algorithm (ALAEN) is proposed here, which introduces stochastic differential mutation and Beta opposition-based learning into the artificial lemming algorithm (ALA). The comparison with other algorithms on the CEC2017 test set shows that it can effectively improve the optimization ability and convergence speed of the artificial lemming algorithm. Among all algorithms, ALA has an overall ranking of 5.45 and ALAEN has a ranking of 1.34. The ability of ALAEN to solve the actual problem of UAV trajectory planning is tested on two different maps, and it is found that it can effectively improve the path planning ability and ensure safety compared with the ALA. In the small map scene, the average cost function of ALA is 92.999, and the average cost function of ALAEN is 91.598, which is a significant improvement. Compared with other algorithms, ALAEN has the shortest trajectory route and trajectory cost function.

title: Ganary: Effectively Protecting GPU Memory with Indexed Canaries
abstract: GPUs have emerged as essential platforms to accelerate compute-intensive applications such as deep learning models and LLMs. However, despite their essentiality, GPU programs still suffer from device stack buffer overflow issues, undermining GPU programs’ security and trustworthiness. Unfortunately, few studies have been devoted to addressing this issue and device stack buffer overflows are often overlooked.

title: Research and Design of a Big Data-Driven Hybrid Weighting Algorithm for the Comprehensive Evaluation of Distance Teaching Platforms
abstract: Comprehensive evaluation of distance teaching platforms remains challenging due to diverse stakeholder demands and high-dimensional, multi-source heterogeneous data. In this paper, we propose a big data-driven evaluation framework centered on a dynamic multi-subject index system. Leveraging the Apache Spark engine, we integrate cross-domain data from academic, financial, and logistics sectors using optimized metadata methods to enhance integration efficiency. The technical core is a hybrid weighting algorithm that fuses an improved Principal Component Analysis (PCA) with the Logarithmic Least Squares Method (LLSM). To overcome traditional PCA's limitations in capturing nonlinear features and handling redundancy, we introduce K-means clustering for pre-classification and incorporate L1 regularization to enforce weight sparsity and identify key indicators. Extensive experiments on recent operational data demonstrate that our algorithm achieves a cumulative variance contribution rate of 94.82% and an evaluation accuracy of 91.34%, significantly outperforming traditional AHP and single-algorithm baselines. A case study identifies platform advantages in teaching quality and critical bottlenecks in market competition, providing a scalable, objective framework for the digital transformation of education groups.

title: Federated Fine-Tuning of Sparsely-Activated Large Language Models on Resource-Constrained Devices
abstract: Federated fine-tuning of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)-based large language models (LLMs) is challenging due to their massive computational requirements and the resource constraints of participants. Existing works attempt to fill this gap through model quantization, computation offloading, or expert pruning. However, they cannot achieve desired performance due to impractical system assumptions and a lack of consideration for MoE-specific characteristics. In this paper, we propose Flux, a system designed to enable federated fine-tuning of MoE-based LLMs across participants with constrained computing resources (e.g., consumer-grade GPUs), aiming to minimize time-to-accuracy. Flux introduces three key innovations: (1) quantization-based local profiling to estimate expert activation with minimal overhead, (2) adaptive layer-aware expert merging to reduce resource consumption while preserving accuracy, and (3) dynamic expert role assignment using an exploration-exploitation strategy to balance tuning and non-tuning experts. Extensive experiments on LLaMA-MoE and DeepSeek-MoE with multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that Flux significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving up to 4.75× speedup in time-to-accuracy.

title: Enhanced Poisson Multi-Bernoulli Filter for Multi-Group Target Split-and-Combine Tracking
abstract: Split-and-Combine processes of dense group targets are critical aspects of group target tracking. However, most existing research is limited to scenarios involving only two target groups, which restricts the practical applicability of these methods. The present study addresses the challenge of tracking multiple group targets that may undergo splitting or combination by introducing an enhanced Poisson multi-Bernoulli (EPMB) filter. The EPMB filter incorporates a possibility-based decision mechanism to identify multi-group split-and-combine events with higher probabilities. Within this framework, multigroup split-and-combine events are generated using a Gibbs-like data association method, and the corresponding possibility values are computed. The selected split-and-combine outcomes are subsequently used to reconstruct the posterior density function (PDF) of the standard Poisson multi-Bernoulli (PMB) filter following the prediction step, thereby enabling an adaptive filtering process that accounts for these events. Simulation experiments conducted in two representative scenarios indicate that the proposed method effectively addresses the challenges of group split-and-combine, and demonstrates superior performance compared to existing approaches. This method may contribute to the development of more robust real-world tracking systems.

title: FedEnD: Communication-efficient Federated Learning for non-IID data via decentralized ensemble distillation
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) offers a paradigm for collaborative AI that mitigates raw data exposure, yet the statistical heterogeneity of client data severely constrains its practical application. This non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) setting induces client drift, leading to unstable optimization and degraded generalization, particularly for under-represented classes. Existing solutions present a difficult trade-off: iterative, regularization-based methods suffer from high communication overhead and a centralized bottleneck, while knowledge-distillation-based approaches rely on impractical artifacts, such as shared public datasets. This work introduces FedEnD , a novel framework that addresses the previous challenge through an efficient, fully decentralized architecture. FedEnD employs a two-stage protocol that decouples local specialist training from a collaborative fusion stage. Following a communication-free training phase, clients perform a one-shot peer-to-peer broadcast that shares (optionally privatized) specialist parameters and lightweight class-count statistics. Each client then uses these statistics to construct a class-distribution-weighted teacher ensemble from the received specialists. Crucially, this ensemble’s knowledge is distilled into a robust global model on each client, using only their local data as unlabeled inputs, obviating the need for a central server or auxiliary data. Extensive experiments on MNIST, FashionMNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that FedEnD outperforms baselines, surpassing robust methods such as SCAFFOLD by +5.7% on complex datasets in pathologically skewed settings. This superior accuracy is achieved while reducing communication bandwidth by 68.6% compared to standard iterative averaging, and by up to 84% compared to gradient-correction methods like SCAFFOLD, highlighting a favorable trade-off between accuracy and communication bandwidth in decentralized learning under severe non-IID partitions.

title: DEKL 2.0: Trace-Indexed Knowledge Evolution in Dependent Type Theory
abstract: DEKL 2.0 is a dependent type-theoretic framework for trace-indexed knowledge evolution. Its central claim is that the proof calculus remains monotone under standard structural rules, while non-monotonic behavior arises semantically from trace extension. Finite and infinite traces are first-class objects in the computational universe; knowledge is interpreted as a presheaf over the finite-trace category; and proposition-level reasoning is handled categorically with fixed-point support. We establish trace--reachability correspondence and completeness, characterize non-monotonicity by non-surjective restriction maps, and present a semantic interpretation based on the free category generated by a transition system. The framework unifies executable traces, typed witnesses, and knowledge revision in one dependent language.

title: HumDial-EIBench: A Human-Recorded Multi-Turn Emotional Intelligence Benchmark for Audio Language Models
abstract: Evaluating the emotional intelligence (EI) of audio language models (ALMs) is critical. However, existing benchmarks mostly rely on synthesized speech, are limited to single-turn interactions, and depend heavily on open-ended scoring. This paper proposes HumDial-EIBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating ALMs' EI. Using real-recorded human dialogues from the ICASSP 2026 HumDial Challenge, it reformulates emotional tracking and causal reasoning into multiple-choice questions with adversarial distractors, mitigating subjective scoring bias for cognitive tasks. It retains the generation of empathetic responses and introduces an acoustic-semantic conflict task to assess robustness against contradictory multimodal signals. Evaluations of eight ALMs reveal that most models struggle with multi-turn emotional tracking and implicit causal reasoning. Furthermore, all models exhibit decoupled textual and acoustic empathy, alongside a severe text-dominance bias during cross-modal conflicts.

title: Razvoj in delovanje umetne inteligence
abstract: V tem besedilu se bomo na seznanili z razvojem in značilnostmi umetne inteligence (UI), ki je postala del našega vsakdanjika. Osredotočili se bomo na generativno UI, kot so ChatGPT in DALL-E, ki spontano prodirajo v izobraževanje in prinašajo priložnosti za individualizacijo učenja ter različne izzive. V prvem delu spoznamo osnove UI – sisteme, ki se učijo iz podatkov. Razlikujemo med ozko UI (današnji specializirani sistemi) in splošno UI (še ne obstaja). Sledil bo zgodovinski pregled od Turingovega testa (1950) do sodobnih transformatorjev. Nadaljevali bomo z generativno UI, ki ustvarja nove vsebine in deluje večmodalno. Razložili bomo, kako veliki jezikovni modeli (LLM) statistično napovedujejo besede, ne razumejo pa sveta vzročno, kar povzroča halucinacije. Opozorili bomo, da UI ni nepristranska in odraža pristranskosti učnih podatkov. Zaključili bomo s ključno nevarnostjo – kognitivnim dolgom, kjer prekomerna odvisnost od UI oslabi kritično mišljenje. Poudarili bomo, da mora UI ostati orodje za razširitev razmišljanja, učitelj pa nepogrešljiv vodja učnega procesa.

These limitations create a strong need for automated and scalable customer interaction systems.

title: KARM: Knowledge-Augmented Reagent Management for Digitalized Biological Supply Chains with an Evolvable Graph
abstract: Effective management of biological reagent supply chains is challenged by product selection complexity, fragmented supplier information, and the demand for cost-effective domestic alternatives. We introduce KARM, a framework centered on a continuously evolving Reagent Knowledge Graph (RKG) that acquires multimodal knowledge from product catalogs, scientific literature, and supplier images via a confidence-weighted pipeline with explicit error-propagation control, parses procurement queries into structured constraint tuples for subgraph retrieval, and employs a Graph Neural Network combining multi-objective cost-of-ownership scoring with graph-derived substitution signals. The RKG evolves through bias-aware procurement feedback, enabling community-validated product equivalence learning. A cold-start module handles newly launched reagents lacking procurement history. On a 500-query biological reagent benchmark, KARM achieves 91.2% constraint match—outperforming monolithic LLM baselines by 22.9% and clarification-enhanced baselines by 15.8%—with cold-start recovery reaching 84.3%. Ablations confirm the necessity of every component for supply chain optimization.

title: SERC-PD: Self-Evaluation and Relative Confidence Based Path-Level Reasoning Decoding for Large Language Models
abstract: Multi-path decoding strategies such as Self-Consistency have become mainstream approaches for enhancing multi-step reasoning in large language models (LLMs). However, these methods rely on answer-level majority voting, which fails to distinguish between logically consistent and inconsistent reasoning paths that happen to produce the same answer. Through systematic analysis, we find that logically inconsistent paths account for 8.2% to 51.3% of generated paths across benchmarks of varying difficulty, with a significant portion accidentally arriving at correct answers. To address this limitation, we propose SERC-PD (Self-Evaluation and Relative Confidence Based Path-level Reasoning Decoding), a training-free inference-time strategy that performs path-level quality assessment. SERC-PD guides the model to evaluate the logical consistency of complete reasoning paths through structured self-evaluation prompts, then applies relative confidence modeling via top-K Softmax normalization to eliminate cross-context probability scale differences. Extensive experiments on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks with five LLMs of different architectures (7B–30B parameters) demonstrate that SERC-PD achieves consistent improvements over Self-Consistency in both accuracy (up to +6.7 percentage points) and logical consistency scores, with the two metrics showing 92% directional agreement across 25 model-dataset combinations, validating our hypothesis that suppressing logically inconsistent paths leads to accuracy improvements.

title: Text Classification and Intelligent Generation of Douyin E-commerce Scripts Based on the Collaboration of FastText and Transformer
abstract: The in-depth integration of Natural Language Processing technology with e-commerce scenarios provides technical support for the efficient classification and personalized generation of e-commerce scripts. To address issues such as low accuracy in text classification and insufficient adaptability of generated text, this study proposes a script text classification and generation model that integrates a Fast Text classification model and a Transformer model. Leveraging the efficient text classification capability of the Fast Text classification model and the Transformer model's ability to dynamically capture semantic associations and user preferences, this model achieves accurate classification and adaptive generation of script texts. In index testing, the model achieved a text classification accuracy of 98.81% on the validation set, with a generation time of 10.17 milliseconds per script text. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model effectively improves the accuracy of Douyin e-commerce script classification and the adaptability of generated content through a multi-technology collaboration mechanism, providing a new path for the intelligent design of scripts in the live-streaming e-commerce field.

title: SwiftFL: Enabling Speculative Training for On-Device Federated Deep Learning
abstract: Federated deep learning (FDL) is a promising privacy-preserving approach for training deep neural networks on distributed datasets without raw data sharing. But the classical synchronous FDL faces straggler problem: slow trainers severely impede overall efficiency. Inspired by speculative execution techniques in modern processors, this paper proposes SwiftFL, a novel and efficient speculative training system for FDL. Instead of simply waiting for slower trainer, SwiftFL proactively updates the global model with predicted gradients, enabling faster trainers to speculatively initiate the next training round. Furthermore, a gradient compensation technique is proposed to correct mispredicted training without re-training. Finally, to overcome the model-drift problem caused by fast trainers perform more local training rounds, we propose a client selection strategy. This strategy determines whether trainers should perform speculative training by striking a balance between two metrics: model drift degree and local training efficiency. In the evaluation, we compare SwiftFL with four state-of-the-art FDL systems and demonstrate that SwiftFL achieves an average speedup of 6.08× while maintaining consistent final model accuracy.

title: Unified Network Embedding via Mutual Fusion of Communities and Roles
abstract: Most network embedding (NE) methods are either based on the proximity for community-guided tasks or on the structural similarity for role-oriented tasks. While being prevalent and effective, there still exists some potential issues that need further attention: 1) community and role are always regarded as orthogonal problems. They have rarely been combined to model the latent structures within the complex network. However, the generation of the network is usually jointly driven by these two mechanisms; and 2) few works study the interaction between roles or communities, which leads to the generation process of the network cannot being effectively modeled. To solve these problems, we propose a unified network embedding framework via mutual fusion of community and role (UMFCR). We combine the Gaussian mixture model (GMM) with a variational graph auto-encoder to generate node embeddings and discover the membership distribution of each node. An elaborate fusion pattern is then designed to produce the generation process for each link from the perspective of both community and role. The promising experimental results on real-world data demonstrate the necessity of fusing these two mechanisms and the superior performance of the model on different network tasks.

title: Optimizing Campus Security Systems: Leveraging Ontologies and Large Language Models to Enhance Detection Accuracy and System Reliability
abstract: Ensuring campus security requires AI-driven anomaly detection systems that are not only accurate, but also interpretable and responsive. This study presents a decisionsupport framework that combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with ontology-driven reasoning and large language models (LLMs) to enhance security monitoring. A controlled experiment involving 30 professional security personnel and 50 simulated scenarios evaluated the system’s effectiveness. The results indicate a significant improvement in anomaly detection accuracy, increasing from 65% (baseline) to $85 {\%}(p=0.027)$, while reducing false alarms. Additionally, response times decreased by $\mathbf{5 2} {\%} \boldsymbol{(} \mathbf{p}=$ 0.001) compared to conventional keyword-based retrieval systems. By integrating structured domain knowledge with adaptive AI reasoning, this approach facilitates precise threat identification and enables faster, well-informed security decisions. These findings demonstrate that ontology-enhanced AI can effectively address key limitations in security monitoring, offering a scalable and interpretable solution for real-time campus safety management.

title: Fully multiplexed photonic tensor computing
abstract: Tensor operations dominate modern computational workloads, yet their further acceleration demands hardware platforms with greater parallelism. Although photonic computing provides a compelling route for parallel processing, fully exploiting all native multiplexing dimensions of optical fields is impeded by the challenges in routing and programming light in all dimensions simultaneously. Here we introduce FieldCore, a fully multiplexed photonic tensor core that jointly harnesses wavelength, radio-frequency, guided-mode, time and space dimensions, thereby enabling parallelism to scale multiplicatively within a single optical field. Enabled by inverse-designed silicon photonics, FieldCore preserves a uniform programmed computation across all multiplexed channels in parallel. Experimentally, we validate and benchmark its performance from ultra-high-baudrate arithmetic operations to high-fidelity image convolution and parallel handwritten-digit recognition. We further use FieldCore to unlock applications that naturally require high-dimensional data processing, such as high-dimensional hyperspectral classification and massively parallel mechanical fault diagnosis. Our FieldCore supports an estimated aggregate compute throughput of 69.12 tera operations per second (TOPS) and accommodates up to 1,800 parallel input streams within a single core, establishing a scalable paradigm for fully multiplexed photonic tensor computing and AI inference.

title: Quantum Noise Reachability Analysis: Multi-Source Error Classification and Correction Recommendation for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
abstract: We introduce noise reachability analysis — a method for determining which physical qubit errors propagate past quantum error correction codes to become logical errors. The engine classifies noise into three source categories (channel, gate, environment) with 12 sub-types, evaluates each against six QEC code families at multiple code distances (720 evaluations per scan), and determines which errors are "reachable" (propagate past the best available correction). We demonstrate automatic noise bias detection, correlated burst noise handling, and noise-aware QEC code selection. The engine recommends optimal codes with 24 source-specific compensating controls beyond code distance increase. Implemented within QCrypton and validated across multiple noise scenarios, the analysis completes in under 2ms.

title: Adaptive Kernel Density Estimation with LSTM for Anomaly Detection in High-Frequency Trading Time Series
abstract: The rapid proliferation of algorithmic trading has introduced sophisticated market manipulation tactics, such as spoofing and layering, posing severe threats to the stability of financial markets. Detecting these anomalies in high-frequency trading (HFT) environments is highly challenging due to the extreme class imbalance and intense heteroskedasticity inherent in microsecond-level limit order book (LOB) data. Traditional machine learning and pure deep learning models often struggle to balance precision and recall under such volatile conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel hybrid anomaly detection framework, AKDE-LSTM, which integrates Adaptive Kernel Density Estimation (AKDE) with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. By dynamically sensing local micro-volatility, the AKDE module extracts high-quality statistical probability distributions as physical priors, which are subsequently fed into the LSTM to capture complex temporal dependencies. Extensive experiments conducted on a real-world, highly imbalanced NASDAQ dataset containing approximately five million tick records demonstrate the overwhelming superiority of the proposed framework. The AKDE-LSTM model achieves an outstanding F1-Score of 0.894 and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.962, significantly outperforming baseline models such as Isolation Forest and standard LSTM. Furthermore, with an average single-step inference latency of merely 1.2 milliseconds, the proposed framework fully satisfies the stringent near real-time processing requirements of modern quantitative trading systems, offering a robust and highly feasible solution for industrial regulatory technology.

title: Investigating Content Moderation in Low-Resource Languages: The Role of Embedding-Guided Sampling, Multi-Task Annotation, and Multi-Modal Context
abstract: Content moderation remains difficult in low-resource languages because abusive content is relatively rare, cultural meaning often depends on context, and high-quality annotation is expensive. This paper examines how three factors affect moderation performance in this setting: embedding-guided sampling, multi-task annotation across toxicity, emotional tone, and topic, and the use of multi-modal context. Using Tigrinya as a case study, we analyze 3,000 comments and compare small fine-tuned models with hosted frontier Large Language Models (LLMs). The results show that careful data selection and richer supervision lead to more robust performance, and that compact specialized models can outperform much larger general-purpose systems. They also indicate that errors are concentrated in comments whose interpretation depends on sarcasm, local political references, and mixed-language context. Taken together, the findings suggest that progress in low-resource moderation depends less on scale alone and more on how data, labels, and context are organized.

title: Cognitive Knowledge Graph Modeling and Personalized Path Recommendation for University Chinese Education
abstract: Semantic modeling of artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated strong adaptability in cognitive education tasks. Based on a knowledge graph (KG) structure, this paper constructs a cognitive map for University Chinese language education, consisting of heterogeneous nodes and multiple semantic relations. A cognitive state reasoning architecture is proposed based on a feedforward neural network (FNN), along with a personalized learning path recommendation algorithm that integrates path scoring and ranking. Both the knowledge graph construction and model training are driven by real learner behavior data. Experimental results show that the graph attention network (GAT) model achieves an F1-score of 0.877 in cognitive state classification, with an average system response time of 84 ms and a path output precision of 88.3%, indicating high effectiveness and responsiveness. This research provides a scalable and intelligent framework for personalized cognitive modeling and adaptive instruction in university-level language education.

title: Dual-Mode Adaptive Memory-Anchored Target State Estimation Based on Shooting Event Triggering under Dense False Measurements
abstract: To address the problem of severe contamination of radar tracking filters by dense projectile false measurements during anti-aircraft weapon firing, which leads to degraded estimation accuracy and even target loss, a dual-mode adaptive memory-anchored state estimation algorithm triggered by shooting events is proposed. Distinguished from conventional probabilistic data association and interacting multiple model methods, the proposed algorithm utilizes the system’s firing signal as a prior temporal trigger condition. During firing periods, it actively suspends measurement updates and switches to a memory-anchored mode based on the mean velocity derived from a dual-buffer sliding window, thereby circumventing false measurement interference at its source. Upon cessation of firing, a linear weighted smooth transition strategy is employed to achieve rapid target reacquisition. Theoretical analysis elucidates the error propagation characteristics of the memory-anchored extrapolation and the influence mechanism of the sliding window length on estimation accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly enhances target state estimation accuracy and reacquisition capability after lock-loss in dense false measurement environments, providing a novel engineering solution for radar anti-projectile interference.

title: Vitiligo state assessment based on progressive transfer learning and multimodal domain adaptation
abstract: Vitiligo is a common skin depigmentation disorder; assessing its state is crucial for the treatment outcome. Collecting multimodal data for vitiligo assessment is complex and costly in clinical practices, and the limited data size restricts the performance of deep learning models. Transfer learning can alleviate the shortage of training data in medical image recognition, however, its applications in vitiligo state assessment are constrained by feature differences between natural and medical images and insufficient generalization to different modalities. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a vitiligo state assessment method based on progressive transfer learning and multimodal domain adaptation. The scheme uses a large set of unlabeled medical images as a bridge to reduce the discrepancies between natural and medical images through multi-step fine-tuning. An adaptive parameter unfreezing strategy is then applied for the accurately labeled target data to improve the adaptability and accuracy of the model. In addition, an integrated multimodal domain adaptation approach based on CycleGAN and hue, saturation, value color space transformation is proposed to reduce the impact of modality differences on transfer learning. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to the conventional transfer learning method, the proposed method improves the accuracy by 2.4% and 3.6% on the clinical and Wood's lamp modality datasets, respectively. This accurate vitiligo state assessment method can be applied to a wide range of multimodal dermatological diseases where labeled data is limited.

title: Artificial intelligence-based reclassification of gastric adenocarcinoma enables prognostic stratification via diffuse-type patch proportion
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastric adenocarcinoma (GAC) remains a major global health burden with marked heterogeneity, complicating diagnosis and prognostic assessment. The Laurén classification, though widely used, suffers from interobserver variability, particularly in defining the mixed subtype. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven image analysis may improve standardization and prognostic assessment in GAC. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 404 patients with resected GAC (2015-2022) from Fundeni Clinical Institute. Whole-slide images (WSIs) were annotated by pathologists with expertise and processed into patches for training a two-stage deep learning pipeline based on YOLO26m-cls. The first model (GAC-I) distinguished malignant from non-malignant tissue, while the second (GAC-ST) classified malignant patches as intestinal or diffuse. We developed the diffuse prognostic score (DPS), defined as the proportion of diffuse patches relative to total patches, and correlated it with overall survival (OS). RESULTS: GAC-I and GAC-ST achieved high diagnostic performances, with accuracies of 0.9437 ± 0.0317 (F1 score: 0.9456 ± 0.0243) and 0.8080 ± 0.0833 (F1 score: 0.7528 ± 0.1094). DPS ≥ 0.5 was significantly associated with lower median OS (16.1 months) compared to DPS < 0.5 (42.067 months), association confirmed by multivariate Cox-regression analysis (HR 3.88, p < 0.001) and matched case-control analysis. Groups were balanced across all variables except tumor differentiation, which was more frequently high-grade in DPS ≥ 0.5. After adjustment, DPS ≥ 0.5 remained an independent predictor of mortality (HR 2.684, p = 0.027). CONCLUSION: We developed and validated a robust AI-based framework for automated GAC classification and prognostic stratification using H&E WSIs. DPS is an independent, reproducible marker of OS, supporting its potential integration into clinical pathology workflows to guide personalized treatment.

title: Fast and Effective Redistricting Optimization via Composite-Move Tabu Search
abstract: Spatial redistricting is a practical combinatorial optimization problem that demands high-quality solutions, rapid turnaround, and flexibility to accommodate multi-criteria objectives and interactive refinement. A central challenge is the contiguity constraint: enforcing contiguity in integer-programming or heuristic search can severely shrink the feasible neighborhood, weaken exploration, and trap the search in poor local optima. We introduce a composite-move Tabu search (CM-Tabu) that systematically expands the feasible neighborhood space in Tabu search while preserving contiguity. When a boundary unit cannot be reassigned individually without disconnecting its district, our method identifies a minimal set of units that can move together, or a pair of units (or sets of units) that can be switched, as a contiguity-preserving composite move. Candidate single-unit and composite moves are generated in linear time by analyzing each district's contiguity graph using articulation points and biconnected components. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach substantially improves solution quality, run-to-run robustness, and computational efficiency relative to traditional Tabu search and other baselines. For example, in the Philadelphia case, the approach can consistently attain the theoretical global optimum in population-equality and support multi-criteria trade-offs. CM-Tabu delivers optimization performance suitable for real-world practices and decision-support workflows.

title: A Systematic Approach for Large Language Models Debugging
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have become central to modern AI workflows, powering applications from open-ended text generation to complex agent-based reasoning. However, debugging these models remains a persistent challenge due to their opaque and probabilistic nature and the difficulty of diagnosing errors across diverse tasks and settings. This paper introduces a systematic approach for LLM debugging that treats models as observable systems, providing structured, model-agnostic methods from issue detection to model refinement. By unifying evaluation, interpretability, and error-analysis practices, our approach enables practitioners to iteratively diagnose model weaknesses, refine prompts and model parameters, and adapt data for fine-tuning or assessment, while remaining effective in contexts where standardized benchmarks and evaluation criteria are lacking. We argue that such a structured methodology not only accelerates troubleshooting but also fosters reproducibility, transparency, and scalability in the deployment of LLM-based systems.

title: Associativity-Peakiness Metric for Contingency Tables
abstract: For the use case of comparing the performance of clustering algorithms whose output is a contingency table, a single performance metric for contingency tables is needed. Such a metric is vital for comparative performance analysis of clustering algorithms. A survey of publicly available literature did not show the presence of such a metric. Metrics do exist for vector pairs of truth values and predicted values, which are an alternative form of output of clustering algorithms. However, the metrics for vector pairs do not reveal the presence of detailed features that are apparent in contingency tables. This paper presents the Associativity Peakiness (AP) metric, which characterizes aspects of clustering algorithm performance that are critical for predicting a clustering algorithm's performance when deployed. The AP metric is analogous to measures of quality for confusion matrices that are outputs of supervised learning algorithms. This paper presents results from simulations in which 500 contingency tables were generated for multiple test scenarios. The results show that for the use case of evaluating clustering algorithms, the AP metric characterizes performance of contingency tables with higher dynamic range than publicly available metrics, and that it is computationally more efficient than comparable publicly available metrics.

title: Open-Ended Video Game Glitch Detection with Agentic Reasoning and Temporal Grounding
abstract: Open-ended video game glitch detection aims to identify glitches in gameplay videos, describe them in natural language, and localize when they occur. Unlike conventional game glitch understanding tasks which have largely been framed as image-level recognition or closed-form question answering, this task requires reasoning about game-specific dynamics such as mechanics, physics, rendering, animation, and expected state transitions directly over continuous gameplay videos and distinguishing true glitches from unusual but valid in-game events. To support this task, we introduce VideoGlitchBench, the first benchmark for open-ended video game glitch detection with temporal localization. VideoGlitchBench contains 5,238 gameplay videos from 120 games, each annotated with detailed glitch descriptions and precise temporal spans, enabling unified evaluation of semantic understanding and temporal grounding. We further propose GliDe, an agentic framework with three key components: a game-aware contextual memory for informed reasoning, a debate-based reflector for multi-perspective glitch detection and verification, and an event-level grounding module that recovers complete glitch intervals from fragmented temporal evidence. We also design a task-specific evaluation protocol that jointly measures semantic fidelity and temporal accuracy. Experiments show that this task remains highly challenging for current multimodal models, while GliDe achieves substantially stronger performance than corresponding vanilla model baselines.

title: Klasifikasi Komentar Judol pada Media Sosial dengan Menggunakan Metode Recurrent Neural Network dan Long Short-Term Memory
abstract: The proliferation of online gambling promotional comments on Indonesian social media has become a serious issue requiring fast and accurate automated handling. This study aims to implement a Hybrid Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) method to classify online gambling comments and compare its performance with standalone RNN and LSTM models. The research utilized a dataset of 10,230 comments subjected to comprehensive preprocessing stages, including the normalization of non-standard language using a slang dictionary. Testing was conducted across three data-splitting scenarios: 90:10, 80:20, and 70:30. Experimental results demonstrate that the standalone LSTM model achieved the highest average accuracy of 97.45%. However, the Hybrid RNN–LSTM model showed significant superiority in terms of performance stability, yielding the lowest standard deviation (0.0027) and the smallest Coefficient of Variation (0.28%) across all scenarios. These findings indicate that while the LSTM architecture is highly effective at capturing short-text context, the Hybrid approach provides better robustness against fluctuations in data proportions, making it highly relevant for implementation as an automated detection system on social media.

title: Low-Power Implementation of Advanced Encryption Standard Using Verilog HDL
abstract: Abstract - The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is a widely used symmetric key encryption algorithm that secures digital data in modern communication systems. Conventional AES hardware implementations often consume high power, limiting their efficiency in resource-constrained environments. This paper presents a low-power AES hardware design implemented in Verilog HDL. The base design uses AES-128 with a 128-bit data block and 128-bit key, while the proposed design enhances security with a 256- bit key. Flip-flop based clock gating is applied to reduce dynamic power by minimizing unnecessary switching activity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed architecture effectively reduces power consumption while maintaining encryption performance, making it suitable for applications in IoT devices, embedded systems, and other low-power environments. Key Words: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), Verilog HDL, Clock Gating, Low-Power Design, Cryptographic Hardware, Power Optimization, AES-128, AES-256.

title: Set-Cover Relaxed Reasoning: A Dual Optimization Framework for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Tuning
abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) often rely on lengthy reasoning chains to improve accuracy in complex tasks, but this leads to severe redundancy, high computational costs, and uncontrollable paths. This paper proposes a novel training/tuning paradigm: Set-Cover Relaxed Reasoning Tuning (SCRT). This method models the reasoning process as a combinatorial optimization problem of "a set of candidate reasoning steps covering the target knowledge requirement," and introduces continuous relaxation (LP Relaxation) of the set coverage to construct a "soft reasoning path." Through a dual variable learning mechanism, the model can automatically learn the "coverage value" of each reasoning step, and achieve adaptive reasoning compression and dynamic termination through structured sparsity. Unlike traditional methods based on length penalties or stopping tokens, SCRT theoretically transforms "whether to continue reasoning" into a provable problem of whether coverage optimization has been satisfied, thus giving the reasoning termination behavior an optimality boundary in an optimization sense.

title: Error Propagation Paths in Quantum Error Correction: A Five-Stage Model for Quantifying Noise Suppression from Physical Source to Logical Qubit
abstract: We introduce a five-stage error propagation path model that traces quantum errors from noise origin through physical qubit, syndrome extraction, QEC decoding, to logical qubit. Each stage carries a quantified error rate. The suppression factor S = log10(p_physical / p_logical) captures QEC effectiveness in a single scalar. We catalog propagation paths across 12 noise types and 6 QEC codes, revealing suppression factors from S > 9 (excellent) to S < 1 (weak/reachable). The model enables bottleneck identification: for a typical superconducting processor, measurement error is the bottleneck (S = 4.0) while all other noise types achieve S > 9. Improving measurement readout by 2x yields 30x improvement in bottleneck logical error rate — more cost-effective than increasing code distance.

title: Application of Deep Learning in Regional Geological Lithological Mapping Based on Multi-source Geophysical, Geochemical and Remote Sensing Data
abstract: Stratigraphic lithology identification and mapping constitute the foundation of geology. Identifying and distinguishing different lithologies is critical for understanding the development and evolution of geological strata. Traditional manual field geological survey is the most accurate method, yet it suffers from low efficiency and high cost. Remote sensing geology is cost-effective and efficient, but performs poorly in covered areas. In this paper, multi-source data including Geophysics, Geochemistry, and Remote Sensing(GGR) are stacked into GeoTIFF files as the sample dataset. A GeoU-Net network model and a predictive segmentation method suitable for regional stratigraphic lithology classification are proposed. The proposed method and system are applied to lithology prediction and segmentation experiments in northern Gansu Province. Compared with manual mapping results, the predicted rock mass distribution is basically consistent, with an accuracy of 91.2%. The model also shows obvious accuracy advantages over other mainstream deep learning-based image segmentation models.

title: Design and Implementation of a Multi-Source Data Fusion and Federated Learning-Based Precision Financial Aid Decision Support System for Universities
abstract: Precision financial aid constitutes a cornerstone of equitable governance in higher education; however, conventional paradigms often struggle with fragmented data exploitation and insufficient privacy-preserving decision-making capabilities. To navigate these bottlenecks, this paper proposes a decision support architecture for university financial aid allocation, leveraging multi-source data fusion and federated learning (FL). Initially, heterogeneous student-centric data are systematically integrated via a unified representation mechanism to achieve a holistic characterization of socio-economic status. Subsequently, a FL framework is orchestrated to facilitate collaborative model training across distributed stakeholders without compromising sensitive information. Building upon this, a data-driven analytical model is developed to ensure the precise and impartial identification of financially marginalized students. Extensive experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed methodology yields superior predictive accuracy while maintaining robust fairness across diverse student cohorts. The empirical results suggest that this system offers a potent, privacy-aware solution for advancing precision financial aid within the higher education landscape.

title: Design of cloud platform for industry-education integration teaching resources based on micro-service architecture and intelligent audit algorithm
abstract: The advancement of intelligent algorithms and microservices architecture has opened new avenues for managing industry-education integration resources. Current resource management faces challenges such as inefficient manual reviews, scalability limitations in traditional monolithic architectures, and high false-negative rates in sensitive information detection. To address these issues, this study designs a cloud-based teaching resource platform with intelligent algorithms tailored for industry-education integration scenarios, aiming to enhance management efficiency and accuracy. The research first developed an intelligent review algorithm integrating video analysis and sensitive word detection. Subsequently, a cloud platform based on microservices architecture was built to enable modular deployment. Experimental results demonstrate that the intelligent review algorithm achieves an F1 value of 0.98, representing a 12.6% improvement over single-mode detection. Sensitive word matching efficiency increases by 47% compared to the traditional Aho-Corasick algorithm. Under high-concurrency conditions, the cloud platform achieves a throughput of 1,890 requests per second, marking an 117% improvement over conventional architectures. This study validates the effectiveness of both the algorithm and platform, providing technical references for efficient management of industry-education integration resources and facilitating the development of a resource-sharing ecosystem for vocational education.

title: A Polar-Coordinate Analytical Localization Method for Moving Targets with Active Multistatic Sonar
abstract: To address the localization challenge of moving targets with active multistatic sonar under the range-only measurement constraint, this paper proposes an analytical polarcoordinate localization algorithm based on elliptical trajectory intersection. Traditional methods for this scenario rely on numerical solutions to bivariate quadratic equation systems, whereas the proposed algorithm directly derives a closed-form analytical solution in the polar-coordinate system, avoiding complex iteration operations and significantly reducing computational complexity. To resolve the ghost solution ambiguity caused by the inherent geometric property of elliptical trajectory intersection, we designed a discrimination strategy based on target motion characteristics, using multi-snapshot clustering and convergence judgment. Meanwhile, to solve the problem that localization results are highly sensitive to time delay error when the target lies on the link between the transmitter and any receiving platform or the target is located near the line of the two receiving platforms, we propose a scheme with three non-collinear receiving platforms and optimal grouping selection to avoid such error-amplified scenarios. Sufficient simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves at least 80% ghost solution elimination probability under nominal conditions, and its computational efficiency is more than 600 times higher than the classical Levenberg-Marquardt (L-M) algorithm while maintaining the same localization accuracy. Furthermore, the adaptive grouping strategy reduces the localization RMSE by more than 45% in error-sensitive scenarios, with no performance loss in low-noise conventional scenarios. The results effectively verify the effectiveness, robustness and superiority of the proposed method.

title: Toeplitz MLP Mixers are Low Complexity, Information-Rich Sequence Models
abstract: Transformer-based large language models are in some respects limited by the quadratic time and space computational complexity of attention. We introduce the Toeplitz MLP Mixer (TMM), a transformer-like architecture that swaps attention for triangular-masked Toeplitz matrix multiplication over the sequence dimension resulting in $\mathcal{O} (dn \log n)$ time and $\mathcal O(dn)$ space complexity during training and $\mathcal O(dn)$ time and space at inference prefill. Despite the lack of sophisticated input modulation or state maintenance present in other sub-quadratic architectures, TMMs yield greater training efficiency in terms of loss achieved per compute and device memory. We demonstrate that TMMs are capable of retaining more input information resulting in improved copying ability, which we argue results from a lack of architectural biases. Consistent with higher input information retention, TMMs exhibit superior information retrieval and in-context learning benchmark accuracy compared to comparable architectures. We conclude with an analysis from the perspective of operator index theory and show that, counterintuitively, trained Toeplitz layers of causal non-invertible models are more likely to be invertible or nearly so than models that are actually invertible over their inputs.

title: Rethinking XAI Evaluation: A Human-Centered Audit of Shapley Benchmarks in High-Stakes Settings
abstract: Shapley values are a cornerstone of explainable AI, yet their proliferation into competing formulations has created a fragmented landscape with little consensus on practical deployment. While theoretical differences are well-documented, evaluation remains reliant on quantitative proxies whose alignment with human utility is unverified. In this work, we use a unified amortized framework to isolate semantic differences between eight Shapley variants under the low-latency constraints of operational risk workflows. We conduct a large-scale empirical evaluation across four risk datasets and a realistic fraud-detection environment involving professional analysts and 3,735 case reviews. Our results reveal a fundamental misalignment: standard quantitative metrics, such as sparsity and faithfulness, are decoupled from human-perceived clarity and decision utility. Furthermore, while no formulation improved objective analyst performance, explanations consistently increased decision confidence, signaling a critical risk of automation bias in high-stakes settings. These findings suggest that current evaluation proxies are insufficient for predicting downstream human impact, and we provide evidence-based guidance for selecting formulations and metrics in operational decision systems.

title: DVGT-2: Vision-Geometry-Action Model for Autonomous Driving at Scale
abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has evolved from the conventional paradigm based on sparse perception into vision-language-action (VLA) models, which focus on learning language descriptions as an auxiliary task to facilitate planning. In this paper, we propose an alternative Vision-Geometry-Action (VGA) paradigm that advocates dense 3D geometry as the critical cue for autonomous driving. As vehicles operate in a 3D world, we think dense 3D geometry provides the most comprehensive information for decision-making. However, most existing geometry reconstruction methods (e.g., DVGT) rely on computationally expensive batch processing of multi-frame inputs and cannot be applied to online planning. To address this, we introduce a streaming Driving Visual Geometry Transformer (DVGT-2), which processes inputs in an online manner and jointly outputs dense geometry and trajectory planning for the current frame. We employ temporal causal attention and cache historical features to support on-the-fly inference. To further enhance efficiency, we propose a sliding-window streaming strategy and use historical caches within a certain interval to avoid repetitive computations. Despite the faster speed, DVGT-2 achieves superior geometry reconstruction performance on various datasets. The same trained DVGT-2 can be directly applied to planning across diverse camera configurations without fine-tuning, including closed-loop NAVSIM and open-loop nuScenes benchmarks.

title: IP-Reasoner: A Unified Integer Programming Framework for Globally Optimal Structured Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Large inference models (LRMs) significantly improve the performance of complex tasks by generating long-chain-of-thought reasoning. However, their inference process is essentially "unstructured and freely generated," lacking global optimality constraints, leading to redundant reasoning, error propagation, and explosive computational overhead. Existing methods (such as Self-Braking Tuning) mainly reduce redundancy through posterior detection or local tuning, but they still do not fundamentally change the reasoning generation mechanism. This paper proposes a novel training and tuning paradigm—IP-Reasoner—which introduces integer programming theory into the modeling of the inference process, treating the inference trajectory as a discrete-structure optimization problem. We are the first to formalize the inference process as a constrained integer optimization problem, ensuring that each inference choice becomes part of the global optimal solution, rather than being generated by local greedy algorithms. This framework incorporates three core innovations: (1) Integer variable encoding of inference paths (Reasoning-as-IP Encoding) (2) Global Consistency Objective (3) Learnable Neural IP Solver Unlike existing methods that only adjust the inference length, our method directly optimizes the "inference structure space," enabling the model to learn how to generate optimal inference paths that satisfy constraints during the training phase, thus naturally avoiding redundancy and error propagation during the inference phase. This paradigm essentially upgrades LRM from a "sequence generation model" to a "structure optimization model," providing a completely new theoretical path for inference modeling.

title: Personal AI Operating Systems: Architectural Foundations, Ethical Assurance, and Commercial Potential in AI-Native Computing
abstract: We are facing a problem with modern computers, which is that the software is getting too complicated. The old ways of managing computer systems are not working well for big and complex systems. This paper is about an idea called Personal AI Operating Systems, which is a big change in how we think about computer systems. It uses something called Large Language Model agents to make the system smarter and able to manage itself. We used an approach to study this new idea, which is called Design Science Research. We compared the ways of doing things with the new ways and we also did a detailed study of how Large Language Models can help with managing computer resources and keeping them secure. What we found out is that Personal AI Operating Systems are really good at planning and understanding what people want to do. They are better than the systems, which can only react to problems. We also looked at the trade-offs between making the system fast and reliable and using machine learning to make decisions. Our results show that Personal AI Operating Systems can make computer systems more resilient and easier to use. Finally we talked about how to make sure that Personal AI Operating Systems are used in a way especially when it comes to peoples personal data. We think that this is an important area and it is going to be worth a lot of money. $56.3 Billion, by 2034.
